title: DUGAE: Unified Geometry and Attribute Enhancement via Spatiotemporal Correlations for G-PCC Compressed Dynamic Point Clouds

AI.tldr: DUGAE is a unified geometry and attribute enhancement framework for G-PCC compressed dynamic point clouds that exploits inter-frame spatiotemporal correlations, achieving substantial BD-PSNR gains and BD-bitrate reductions over GeS-TM v10 and outperforming V-PCC.
AI.motivation: Existing post-decoding quality enhancement methods for point clouds are designed for static data and process frames independently, failing to exploit inter-frame spatiotemporal correlations in dynamic sequences.
AI.method: The framework combines a dynamic geometry enhancement network (DGE-Net) using sparse convolution and feature-domain geometry motion compensation, a detail-aware k-nearest neighbors (DA-KNN) recoloring module at the encoder side, and a dynamic attribute enhancement network (DAE-Net) with temporal feature extraction and feature-domain attribute motion compensation.
AI.result: On seven dynamic point clouds from 8iVFB v2, Owlii, and MVUB, DUGAE improves GeS-TM v10 by an average 11.03 dB BD-PSNR and 93.95% BD-bitrate reduction for D1 geometry, and 4.23 dB BD-PSNR with 66.61% BD-bitrate reduction for luma, while improving PCQM perceptual quality and outperforming V-PCC.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling spatiotemporal correlations in both geometry and attributes provides a unified and effective post-decoding enhancement solution for compressed dynamic point clouds.

title: Structures preserved by primitive actions of $S_ω$

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a P vs. NP-complete complexity dichotomy for constraint satisfaction problems on structures preserved by primitive actions of S_omega = Sym(N).
AI.motivation: Characterizing the computational complexity of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) for infinite-domain structures preserved by primitive actions of Sym(N) requires classifying when such structures can primitively positively construct all finite structures.
AI.method: The authors analyze first-order reducts of the Johnson graph J(k) for k >= 2, whose automorphism group G is the action of Sym(N) on k-element subsets of N, using the existence of a finitely bounded homogeneous Ramsey expansion of J(k) and the fact that G is a maximal closed subgroup of Sym(V).
AI.result: Any structure A preserved by primitive actions of Sym(N) either primitively positively constructs all finite structures (making its CSP NP-complete) or has a CSP solvable in polynomial time (P).
AI.conclusion: The result resolves the CSP complexity dichotomy for the class of structures preserved by primitive actions of Sym(N).

title: Stiefel Manifold Dynamical Systems for Tracking Representational Drift

AI.tldr: The authors introduce Stiefel Manifold Dynamical Systems (SMDS), which track representational drift in neural recordings by allowing orthonormal emission matrices to evolve smoothly across trials on the Stiefel manifold.
AI.motivation: Standard linear dynamical systems (LDS) assume a static mapping from latent states to neural activity, which prevents them from capturing gradual representational drift across trials.
AI.method: SMDS constrains emission matrices to be orthonormal and evolve smoothly over trials on the Stiefel manifold while sharing latent dynamics parameters across trials.
AI.result: Evaluated on simulated datasets and multi-species neural recordings, SMDS consistently outperforms LDS in log-likelihood, requires fewer latent dimensions, reveals gradual drift over minutes, and uncovers slower drift in behaviorally and neurally significant dimensions.
AI.conclusion: SMDS provides an interpretable and accurate framework for quantifying representational drift and modeling nonstationary neural dynamics.

title: Task-Wise Winner Taking Continual Learning

AI.tldr: Task-wise winner-taking continual learning (TWC) improves upon elastic weight consolidation (EWC) by using task-wise Fisher information, a recovering factor, and winner-taking regularization to reduce catastrophic forgetting and distribute parameters across tasks.
AI.motivation: Regularization-based continual learning methods avoid data storage and model expansion, but still suffer from catastrophic forgetting, performance degradation on earlier tasks, and poor parameter distribution across tasks due to limited parameter capacity.
AI.method: TWC computes Fisher information in a task-wise manner, introduces a recovering factor to restore degraded performance on previously trained tasks, and applies winner-taking regularization to allocate weights more effectively across multiple tasks.
AI.result: Experimental results across various continual learning settings show that TWC outperforms up-to-date baseline methods.
AI.conclusion: Task-wise regularization combined with performance recovery and winner-taking weight allocation enables more effective continual learning within a fixed-capacity model.

title: Local Background Features Matter in Out-of-Distribution Detection

AI.tldr: This study proposes a local background feature fine-tuning framework for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection that suppresses background-induced overconfidence using only in-distribution images.
AI.motivation: Deep neural networks often produce overconfident predictions on OOD data, and existing mitigation methods rely on auxiliary OOD datasets, synthetic OOD image generation, or extra model branches.
AI.method: The framework extracts local features with low ground-truth class probability from in-distribution images as background-like targets and applies a margin-based L2-norm loss to suppress their activation magnitude alongside standard cross-entropy loss.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on standard OOD detection benchmarks show that the method is compatible with existing post hoc scoring functions and achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance without auxiliary OOD data or segmentation models.
AI.conclusion: Regularizing local background features directly from in-distribution data offers a simple, self-contained way to reduce OOD overconfidence.

title: Mistake Gating Leads to Energy and Memory Efficient Continual Learning

AI.tldr: Memorized mistake-gated learning restricts synaptic updates to current and past classification errors, cutting parameter updates by 50% to 80% while improving continual and online learning efficiency.
AI.motivation: Artificial neural networks waste energy and memory by updating parameters on every sample, even when already classified correctly, unlike biological systems where plasticity is metabolically expensive.
AI.method: Inspired by negativity bias and error-related negativity, the proposed plasticity rule gates synaptic updates strictly by current and past classification errors, requiring no extra hyperparameters and minimal code.
AI.result: Mistake gating reduces the number of network updates by 50% to 80%, decreases required replay buffer sizes in online learning, and improves robustness on imbalanced classes with negligible computational overhead.
AI.conclusion: Error-gated plasticity provides an energy- and memory-efficient, biologically plausible modification to standard learning rules for continual learning.

title: A Dynamical Systems Analysis of Sequential Hopfield Networks With Softmax Activation

AI.tldr: The authors develop a rigorous dynamical systems analysis of sequential Hopfield networks with low-temperature softmax activation, characterizing oscillation amplitudes and escape times.
AI.motivation: Sequential Hopfield networks use slowly evolving auxiliary variables to trigger transitions between memories, but prior mathematical analyses focused on storage capacity rather than explicit dynamical behavior.
AI.method: Focusing on orthogonal memories, the authors apply geometric singular perturbation theory and fixed-point analysis to simplify the coupled network and slow-variable dynamics under low-temperature softmax activation.
AI.result: The analysis yields precise characterizations of oscillation amplitudes, escape times, and other key dynamical features, and numerical experiments confirm that these findings remain informative for standard random memory setups.
AI.conclusion: Geometric singular perturbation theory provides an effective analytical tool for understanding autonomous state transitions in sequential associative memory models.

title: Behavioral Latency as Weak Event-Time Supervision for EEG Reaction-Time Decoding

AI.tldr: Reformulating single-trial EEG reaction-time decoding as event-time posterior modeling improves prediction accuracy and interpretability over scalar regression on the Healthy Brain Network task.
AI.motivation: Conventional EEG reaction-time decoding treats reaction time as a scalar regression target on a fixed stimulus-locked window, ignoring its role as timing evidence about latent response-relevant dynamics.
AI.method: The model estimates a posterior distribution p(t_event | X) over response-relevant event times and uses the posterior mean as the reaction-time estimate, combined with shifted-crop inference and shift-jitter training to diagnose temporal localization versus scalar shortcuts.
AI.result: Under a subject-disjoint, release-separated protocol on the Healthy Brain Network contrast change detection EEG task across five seeds and four temporal backbones, distributional event-time supervision consistently outperforms scalar regression and temporal-readout controls, while shift-jitter improves shifted-crop robustness.
AI.conclusion: Event-time posterior modeling offers a probabilistic, interpretable formulation for linking single-trial EEG dynamics to behavioral timing, though an equivariance gap remains relative to ideal crop-relative localization.

title: Prior Preferences in Active Inference Agents: Soft, Hard, and Goal Shaping

AI.tldr: This work compares four ways of specifying prior preference distributions in active inference agents, finding that goal shaping maximizes task performance at the expense of learning environment transition dynamics.
AI.motivation: Although prior preference distributions define an active inference agent's exploitative drive via Kullback-Leibler divergence in expected free energy, little attention has been paid to how different preference specifications affect inference and learning.
AI.method: The authors evaluate four preference designs combining hard versus soft goals and the presence or absence of goal shaping (intermediate goals) on a grid world navigation task.
AI.result: Goal shaping achieves the best overall task performance by promoting exploitation, but it hampers exploration and reduces learning of the environment's transition dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Designing prior preferences in active inference involves a direct trade-off between exploitation-driven performance via goal shaping and exploratory learning of environment dynamics.

title: Dual Causal Inference: Integrating Backdoor Adjustment and Instrumental Variable Learning for Medical VQA

AI.tldr: Dual Causal Inference (DCI) integrates Backdoor Adjustment and Instrumental Variable learning in a unified framework for Medical VQA, outperforming existing methods on four benchmarks especially under out-of-distribution settings.
AI.motivation: Medical Visual Question Answering (MedVQA) models often overfit to superficial cross-modal correlations and suffer from both observable and unobserved confounding biases, undermining diagnostic reliability.
AI.method: DCI formulates a Structural Causal Model that mitigates observable cross-modal biases via Backdoor Adjustment while compensating for unobserved confounders using an Instrumental Variable learned from a shared latent space under mutual information constraints.
AI.result: Experiments on SLAKE, SLAKE-CP, VQA-RAD, and PathVQA show that DCI consistently outperforms existing approaches, particularly in out-of-distribution generalization, and qualitative analyses confirm improved interpretability and robustness.
AI.conclusion: Jointly addressing observable and unobserved confounders through dual causal mechanisms enables more trustworthy and deconfounded cross-modal reasoning in MedVQA.

title: VGD: Visual Geometry Gaussian Splatting for Feed-Forward Surround-view Driving Reconstruction

AI.tldr: Visual Gaussian Driving (VGD) is a feed-forward end-to-end framework for surround-view driving scene reconstruction that distills geometric priors from VGGT to improve novel-view rendering quality on nuScenes.
AI.motivation: Feed-forward surround-view driving reconstruction struggles to maintain geometric consistency and high novel-view quality because surround-view cameras have minimal overlap regions.
AI.method: VGD uses a lightweight VGGT variant to distill geometric priors into a geometry branch, a shared-backbone Gaussian Head that fuses multi-scale geometry tokens to predict Gaussian parameters, and joint supervision of a semantic refinement model using multi-scale features from both branches.
AI.result: Experiments on nuScenes demonstrate that VGD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both objective metrics and subjective quality across multiple settings.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly learning and distilling geometric priors to guide semantic refinement enables scalable, high-fidelity feed-forward surround-view reconstruction.

title: Rethinking Facial Expression Recognition in the Era of Multimodal Large Language Models: Benchmark, Datasets, and Beyond

AI.tldr: The authors introduce FERBench to evaluate 20 MLLMs on facial expression recognition, curate two large-scale reasoning datasets, and train UniFER-7B to outperform larger generalist MLLMs.
AI.motivation: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) show promise when facial expression recognition (FER) is framed as VQA, their reasoning and interpretability on FER tasks remain largely unexplored and limited.
AI.method: The authors build FERBench across four FER datasets, curate UniFER-CoT-230K for cold-start initialization and UniFER-RLVR-360K for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), and train a unified model named UniFER-7B.
AI.result: Evaluating 20 MLLMs on FERBench reveals strong classification but weak reasoning; post-training produces UniFER-7B, which outperforms open-source and closed-source generalist MLLMs including Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B.
AI.conclusion: Targeted CoT and RLVR post-training substantially improves the facial expression reasoning and interpretability of MLLMs.

title: Class Agnostic Instance-Level Descriptor for Instance Search

AI.tldr: This paper models instance-level region discovery as hierarchical decomposition of self-supervised ViT features, creating a class-agnostic descriptor that unifies image retrieval, instance search, and multi-instance search.
AI.motivation: Visual instance search lacks effective instance-level representations, and supervised or weakly supervised object detectors generalize poorly to unknown object categories.
AI.method: Using features from a self-supervised ViT, the method hierarchically detects compact feature subsets corresponding to instance regions at multiple granularities (non-leaf and leaf nodes), producing uniform-length descriptors that handle occlusion and object embedding.
AI.result: Empirical studies on three benchmarks show that the descriptor remains effective on both known and unknown object categories and achieves superior performance on single-instance search, multi-instance search, and image retrieval.
AI.conclusion: Hierarchical decomposition of self-supervised ViT features provides a unified, class-agnostic representation for diverse instance-level retrieval tasks.

title: Gray bats heighten their response to social cues when navigating group flight in environments with obstacles

AI.tldr: Stereoscopic video tracking and agent-based modeling of wild gray bats show that bats stay close to walls but increase social repulsion when navigating groups around novel obstacles.
AI.motivation: Echolocation-based group flight in cluttered environments poses acoustic and navigational challenges, yet how bats weigh social versus environmental cues when facing obstacles was unknown.
AI.method: The authors collected stereoscopic video data from a wild colony of gray bats (Myotis grisescens) navigating foraging paths with novel obstacles and built a data-informed agent-based model to infer interaction rules.
AI.result: Bats tend to fly close to walls while spacing out in groups, and the agent-based model reveals that social repulsive behavior is strengthened when navigating novel obstacles.
AI.conclusion: Gray bats adaptively heighten their response to social cues to avoid collisions and manage clutter during group flight around obstacles.

title: Reversible Primitive–Composition Alignment for Continual Vision–Language Learning

AI.tldr: Compo-ReAlign is a continual vision-language learning head that preserves compositional structure and zero-shot performance using a reversible composer, multi-positive InfoNCE, and a spectral trust region.
AI.motivation: Under sequential adaptation without task IDs and with tight rehearsal budgets, vision-language models often retain primitive recognition while losing compositional structure.
AI.method: Compo-ReAlign introduces a reversible composer mapping primitive embeddings to compositions, a multi-positive InfoNCE loss aligning textual and composed views, and a spectral trust region that clips updates when alignment sensitivity inflates.
AI.result: Across compositional DIL and multi-domain MTIL retrieval, Compo-ReAlign sets a new state of the art, improving over the strongest prior by +2.4 R@1 and reducing forgetting by 40%.
AI.conclusion: A compact, reversible alignment head with geometry-aware training enables compositionally robust continual vision-language learning.

title: GarmentGPT: Compositional Garment Pattern Generation via Discrete Latent Tokenization

AI.tldr: GarmentGPT tokenizes sewing pattern boundary curves into discrete latent codes via RVQ-VAE and uses a fine-tuned Vision-Language Model to autoregressively generate compositional garment patterns.
AI.motivation: Manual sewing pattern creation is a bottleneck for digital garment production, while existing generative models either replicate data without structural understanding or struggle to regress raw floating-point coordinates.
AI.method: GarmentGPT uses an RVQ-VAE to tokenize continuous boundary curves into discrete codebook indices and fine-tunes a Vision-Language Model to predict these tokens autoregressively, supported by a Data Curation Pipeline synthesizing over one million images paired with GarmentCode and the Real-Garments Benchmark.
AI.result: Experiments on structured datasets show GarmentGPT achieves 95.62% Panel Accuracy and 81.84% Stitch Accuracy, significantly outperforming existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Discrete latent tokenization aligns garment pattern generation with the symbolic, compositional reasoning capabilities of large language models.

title: RESA: Bringing Back What Sparse Attention Ignores with Residual Estimation

AI.tldr: RESA is a training-free framework that compensates for dropped KV pairs in sparse attention by estimating a rank-1 low-rank prior of attention logits during prefilling and fusing it online during decoding.
AI.motivation: Sparse attention reduces long-context KV cache bottlenecks by selecting critical KVs, but discarding remaining KVs degrades model quality in less sparse scenarios.
AI.method: Based on SVD analysis showing spectral dominance and linear scaling of attention logits, RESA uses a Prior Estimator to derive a rank-1 prior distribution from a typical query at the end of prefilling and an Online Aggregator to fuse it with sparse attention at each decoding step.
AI.result: Without extra training overhead, RESA improves model quality by up to 26% over state-of-the-art baselines at the same KV budget, or maintains quality with up to 33.2% KV budget reduction and 1.23x attention throughput improvement.
AI.conclusion: Exploiting the low-rank redundancy of attention logits as a residual prior effectively recovers information lost in sparse attention.

title: TimeSeg: An Information-Theoretic Segment-Wise Explainer for Time-Series Predictions

AI.tldr: TimeSeg is an information-theoretic, reinforcement-learning-based explainer that selects contiguous time-series subsequences maximizing joint mutual information with target predictions.
AI.motivation: Existing time-series explanation methods either focus on fragmented point-wise attributions or lack principled definitions for meaningful temporal segments.
AI.method: TimeSeg formalizes segment-wise explanation as selecting contiguous subsequences that maximize joint mutual information with the model's prediction, using reinforcement learning to sequentially identify predictive segments per instance.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that TimeSeg produces more coherent, human-understandable explanations while matching or surpassing existing methods on downstream tasks using the identified segments.
AI.conclusion: Information-theoretic reinforcement learning provides a principled way to generate holistic, segment-wise explanations for black-box time-series models.

title: Teaching VLMs to Admit Uncertainty in OCR from Lossy Visual Inputs

AI.tldr: The authors propose uncertainty-aware OCR for degraded documents, training a VLM with GRPO to bracket unreliable spans with uncertainty tags while maintaining transcription accuracy.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models trained solely for accuracy tend to hallucinate fluent but incorrect text on lossy or degraded document images without signaling uncertainty.
AI.method: Using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a pseudo-labeled cold start and a multi-objective reward balancing transcription accuracy and uncertainty coverage, the model learns to wrap uncertain spans in tags; the authors also introduce the Blur-OCR benchmark.
AI.result: On degraded document images, the model maintains transcription accuracy while achieving an uncertainty tag F1 score of 0.685.
AI.conclusion: Rewarding explicit uncertainty tagging during RL post-training improves the trustworthiness and reliability of VLM-based OCR on lossy visual inputs.

title: Predictive CVaR Q-learning

AI.tldr: Predictive CVaR Q-learning introduces a recursive predictive tail value function that uses entire sample trajectories rather than only worst-case outcomes to improve sample efficiency in risk-sensitive RL.
AI.motivation: Existing Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) Q-learning methods suffer from poor sample efficiency and theoretical inconsistencies because they rely heavily on worst-case outcomes and lack a standard recursive Bellman structure.
AI.method: The authors formulate a predictive tail value function admitting a recursive Bellman-like structure, derive a Bellman optimality equation and policy improvement theorem, and use all sample trajectories for updates.
AI.result: Empirical evaluations show that the algorithm consistently improves CVaR performance while maintaining stable and interpretable learning dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The recursive predictive tail value formulation provides sound theoretical foundations and higher sample efficiency for risk-sensitive reinforcement learning.

title: Path Matters: Unveiling Geometric Implicit Bias via Curvature-Aware Sparse View Optimization

AI.tldr: This paper identifies curvature-demand and trajectory-smoothness implicit biases in sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting and proposes curvature-aware trajectory optimization with synthetic view generation.
AI.motivation: In sparse-view settings, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) suffers from geometric inaccuracies, cross-view inconsistencies, and degraded rendering quality.
AI.method: The authors uncover that sparse-view 3DGS demands stronger supervision in high-curvature regions and is sensitive to camera trajectory smoothness, then propose optimizing camera trajectories to maximize curvature coverage with smooth motion alongside synthetic view generation.
AI.result: Experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, DTU, Blender, Tanks & Temples, and LLFF show substantial improvements over state-of-the-art sparse-view methods in both rendering quality and geometric fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Accounting for geometric implicit biases through curvature-aware trajectory planning and synthetic views significantly strengthens sparse-view 3DGS reconstruction.

title: Towards Knowledge‑and‑Data‑Driven Organic Reaction Prediction: RAG‑Enhanced and Reasoning‑Powered Hybrid System with LLMs

AI.tldr: Reaction-Thinker is a hybrid organic reaction prediction system combining RAG-based SFT and GRPO-optimized chain-of-thought reasoning to outperform existing LLMs and task-specific models.
AI.motivation: Purely data-driven organic reaction prediction models and LLMs suffer from limited interpretability and performance bottlenecks.
AI.method: Reaction-Thinker builds a similar-case retrieval database to train a RAG-based LLM via SFT, constructs a reaction reasoning CoT dataset, and trains a reasoning LLM with SFT followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
AI.result: Experiments show Reaction-Thinker achieves the highest Exact Match accuracy and fingerprint similarity (FTS) among compared LLMs and task-specific models, with ablations showing 7.5% and 13.9% relative accuracy gains from RAG and GRPO respectively.
AI.conclusion: Integrating retrieval-augmented knowledge with RL-refined reasoning improves both accuracy and interpretability in organic reaction prediction.

title: Understanding the Dynamics of Forgetting and Generalization in Continual Learning via the Neural Tangent Kernel

AI.tldr: Using Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) theory, the authors analyze continual learning dynamics and propose OGD+ and Orthogonal Penalized Gradient Descent (OPGD) to jointly reduce forgetting and improve generalization.
AI.motivation: Prior continual learning theory focuses on converged models or restrictive distributions, failing to capture intermediate training dynamics or establish two-sided population risk bounds for forgetting.
AI.method: Within the NTK regime, the authors characterize intermediate training via kernel gradient flow and Rademacher complexity bounds, showing that smaller loss Lipschitz constants and cross-task kernels reduce forgetting; they then propose OGD+ (orthogonal gradient projection onto prior samples) and OPGD (adding gradient-norm penalization).
AI.result: Experiments on multiple benchmarks corroborate the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of OPGD.
AI.conclusion: NTK-based analysis of training-time dynamics provides a principled bridge from continual learning theory to practical gradient-projection algorithms.

title: Counterfactual Structural Causal Bandits

AI.tldr: This paper introduces counterfactual structural causal bandits (ctf-SCB), extending bandit action spaces beyond observational and interventional arms to include realizable counterfactual actions.
AI.motivation: Existing causal bandit algorithms operate only at the observational (L1) and interventional (L2) levels of the Pearl Causal Hierarchy, excluding counterfactual (L3) quantities due to perceived inaccessibility.
AI.method: The authors formalize the ctf-SCB framework by expanding the agent's feasible action space to incorporate a class of realizable counterfactual actions.
AI.result: The paper establishes a principled extension of structural causal bandits that integrates L3 counterfactual reasoning into sequential decision-making.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating realizable counterfactual actions opens a new direction for causal bandit algorithms across all levels of the Pearl Causal Hierarchy.

title: Gogo: Group-wise granularity-ordered codec for stable and efficient speech generation

AI.tldr: Gogo is a group-wise granularity-ordered speech codec paired with GogoSpeech, a two-stage speech language model with a GRPO-trained adaptive token allocator, achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction and long-form TTS.
AI.motivation: Speech language models require codecs that balance high-level semantic abstraction for autoregressive modeling with fine-grained acoustic detail, while accounting for non-uniform information density in speech.
AI.method: Gogo quantizes frame groups into coarse-to-fine tokens, GogoSpeech generates a coarse backbone at a low token rate before adding fine details, and a GRPO-trained token allocator dynamically assigns token budgets based on group complexity.
AI.result: Gogo achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction across most metrics at a token rate of 47, and GogoSpeech reduces average token rates while attaining state-of-the-art results in zero-shot and long-form TTS.
AI.conclusion: Granularity-ordered tokenization with adaptive RL-based budget allocation enables both efficient and high-quality speech generation.

title: Horseshoe Splatting: Handling Structural Sparsity for Uncertainty-Aware Gaussian-Splatting Radiance Field Rendering

AI.tldr: Horseshoe Splatting applies a global-local Horseshoe prior to 3D Gaussian Splatting covariances via factorized variational inference, delivering calibrated pixel-wise uncertainty and theoretical contraction guarantees.
AI.motivation: Existing 3DGS pipelines are deterministic and do not enforce structural sparsity in per-splat covariances, leaving noise-dominated components under-regularized and lacking predictive uncertainty.
AI.method: The authors place a global-local Horseshoe prior on covariance scales and fit the model with factorized variational inference using inverse-Gamma augmentation, enabling Monte Carlo rendering of pixel-wise posterior uncertainty.
AI.result: Theoretical analysis establishes posterior contraction rates transferred to rendered images via a local Lipschitz mapping, while experiments show high-quality uncertainty maps alongside state-of-the-art 3DGS visual fidelity and runtime.
AI.conclusion: Horseshoe Splatting provides a theoretically grounded, uncertainty-aware 3DGS renderer that handles structured covariance sparsity with minimal overhead.

title: R4: Nested Reasoning-Retrieval for Reward Modeling in Role-Playing Agents

AI.tldr: R4 equips both a reward model and a role-playing agent with nested reasoning and retrieval capabilities, improving persona fidelity, narrative coherence, and emotional expressiveness.
AI.motivation: Current LLMs and standard RAG or scalar-reward RL approaches often produce literal, bland dialogue that fails to sustain nuanced character personas and contextual grounding in role-playing.
AI.method: R4 reformulates reward modeling as structured multi-step reasoning integrated with retrieved knowledge, and uses this reward supervision in RL to train a dialogue agent with matching reasoning and retrieval capabilities.
AI.result: Experiments show substantial gains in persona fidelity, narrative coherence, and emotional expressiveness, with agents demonstrating more effective retrieval and retrieval-informed self-reflection.
AI.conclusion: Dual reasoning-retrieval reward modeling enables emergent, contextually grounded role-playing behaviors beyond prior scalar-reward methods.

title: ORION: Decoupling and Alignment for Unified Autoregressive Understanding and Generation

AI.tldr: ORION resolves the semantic-structural conflict in monolithic autoregressive multimodal LLMs using a non-linear vision head for decoupling and a Representation Consistency Loss for semantic alignment.
AI.motivation: Monolithic autoregressive MLLMs suffer from catastrophic forgetting of high-level semantic understanding when optimized for low-level reconstructability in visual generation.
AI.method: ORION decouples structural generation pressures from shared representations via a non-linear vision head, aligns semantics during generation with a Representation Consistency Loss, and uses a progressive training recipe without task-specific separate parameters.
AI.result: Built purely on a monolithic autoregressive backbone, ORION matches or exceeds recent state-of-the-art unified models that rely on more complex architectures.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling and alignment allow simple monolithic autoregressive architectures to unify multimodal understanding and generation effectively.

title: Operator Theory-Driven Autoformulation of MDPs for Control of Queueing Systems

AI.tldr: This work proposes an operator-theoretic LLM autoformulation framework that models queueing MDPs as graphs of event-based Bellman operators, shrinking the search space and identifying optimal policy structures.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM autoformulation targets one-shot optimization rather than sequential Markov decision processes (MDPs), which have much larger formulation search spaces and require interpretable policy structure analysis.
AI.method: The framework represents the Bellman equation as a graph of interpretable event operators (e.g., arrival, departure, routing) constrained by a universal three-level topology, uses customized Monte Carlo tree search with solver feedback and syntax checking to build graphs, and applies a low-complexity algorithm to detect threshold-like policy structures.
AI.result: Numerical results demonstrate effective automatic formulation of queueing problems and accurate identification of structural policy properties.
AI.conclusion: Operator-graph representations make LLM-driven autoformulation tractable and interpretable for sequential queueing control problems.

title: Preference-based Policy Optimization from Sparse-reward Offline Dataset

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a contrastive preference learning method for sparse-reward offline RL that bypasses value function estimation and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
AI.motivation: In sparse-reward offline RL, learned value functions often become overly optimistic on poorly represented state-action pairs, causing overestimation bias and degraded policies.
AI.method: Instead of estimating value functions directly, the method trains policies via contrastive preference learning that contrasts successful demonstrations against both in-dataset failure behaviors and synthetic out-of-support behaviors.
AI.result: Empirical evaluations on challenging sparse-reward offline RL benchmarks show substantial improvements over existing state-of-the-art baselines in both learning efficiency and final performance.
AI.conclusion: Contrastive preference learning with out-of-support negatives offers a robust, value-free alternative for sparse-reward offline RL.

title: CLIP-FMoE: Scalable CLIP via Fused Mixture-of-Experts with Enforced Specialization

AI.tldr: CLIP-FMoE integrates Mixture-of-Experts into CLIP fine-tuning using Isolated Constrained Contrastive Learning and a Fusion Gate to improve downstream tasks while preserving zero-shot capabilities.
AI.motivation: Existing MoE adaptations for CLIP suffer from high computational overhead during sequential training and degradation of pre-trained zero-shot performance.
AI.method: CLIP-FMoE trains specialized experts on cluster-based data partitions via Isolated Constrained Contrastive Learning to speed up specialization, and uses a Fusion Gate mechanism to prevent catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks show consistent downstream improvements, preserved zero-shot capabilities, and robust performance across varying context lengths.
AI.conclusion: Enforced expert specialization paired with gated fusion enables scalable, forgetting-resistant MoE fine-tuning for CLIP.

title: Correlated Policy Optimization in Multi-Agent Subteams

AI.tldr: This paper formalizes subteam-based coordination in cooperative multi-agent RL using Bayesian networks and introduces a dynamic subteam construction heuristic that outperforms standard baselines.
AI.motivation: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning faces exponential scalability bottlenecks in joint action and observation spaces.
AI.method: Inspired by human teams, the authors partition agents into correlated subgroups with limited inter-group interaction, formalize correlated joint policies via directed acyclic graphs, prove convergence of regularized policy gradient ascent under decomposability, and propose a heuristic for dynamic context-aware subteams.
AI.result: Across multiple benchmark environments, the proposed method outperforms standard multi-agent RL baselines.
AI.conclusion: Modeling structured subteam correlations via Bayesian networks provides a scalable and theoretically grounded approach to cooperative MARL.

title: Sample Lottery: Unsupervised Discovery of Critical Instances for LLM Reasoning

AI.tldr: CONST is an unsupervised sample-selection framework for LLM reasoning that uses procedural and outcome volatility with conformal prediction to identify critical training instances without ground-truth answers.
AI.motivation: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Reward (RLVR) typically requires full dataset annotation and uniform compute allocation, even though a small subset of samples may suffice.
AI.method: Under the lottery sample hypothesis, Complementary Conformal Selection (CONST) scores unlabeled samples by procedural volatility (reasoning variations) and outcome volatility (final answer inconsistencies), then uses conformal prediction set cardinality to select instances for annotation.
AI.result: Theoretical analysis shows CONST approximates the optimal policy, and extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and datasets demonstrate its effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: Unsupervised volatility-based conformal selection enables data-efficient RLVR by focusing annotation on critical reasoning instances.

title: XIL: Cross-Expanding Incremental Learning

AI.tldr: The authors introduce Cross-Expanding Incremental Learning (XIL), the BiDoT Score metric, and the XEED framework to handle class-incremental learning across evolving domains.
AI.motivation: Traditional class-incremental learning (CIL) assumes a single shared domain, failing when new classes arrive from distinct domains and require bidirectional domain transferability (BiDoT).
AI.method: Semantic Expansion through Evolving Domains (XEED) combines domain-specialized prompts, residual-guided representation modulation, and evolving prototype embeddings to expand class semantics bidirectionally across domains, evaluated with the new BiDoT Score.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on benchmarks with significant domain shifts show XEED outperforms existing CIL baselines by a large margin in both standard accuracy and BiDoT scores.
AI.conclusion: XIL and XEED establish a foundation for continual learning in realistic settings where both classes and domains evolve together.

title: Smarter Not Harder: Generative Process Evaluation with Intrinsic-Signal Driving and Ability‑Adaptive Reward Shaping

AI.tldr: TP-GRPO improves RL training of large reasoning models using intrinsic-signal-driven process evaluation, thought-level reward granularity, and difficulty-aware reward shaping.
AI.motivation: Outcome-only rewards provide sparse feedback for large reasoning models, while existing generative process reward models (GenPRMs) rely heavily on their own reasoning ability, suppress exploration, and are vulnerable to reward hacking.
AI.method: TP-GRPO judges reasoning steps using semantic cues from the solution (intrinsic-signal-driven evaluation), assigns rewards at thought-level granularity to avoid over-dense feedback, and applies difficulty-aware reward shaping targeting key tokens.
AI.result: Experiments on 1.5B and 7B large reasoning models show TP-GRPO achieves higher accuracy improvements while using significantly fewer training samples than baselines.
AI.conclusion: Intrinsic-signal-driven, thought-level process rewards make RL training of reasoning models more sample-efficient and resistant to reward hacking.

title: On the Computational Limits of AI4S-RL : A Unified $\varepsilon$-$N$ Analysis

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a unified epsilon-N framework quantifying the minimal computational cost required for AI-for-Science (AI4S) surrogate simulators to guarantee unbiased tabular RL value estimation.
AI.motivation: Replacing expensive PDE solvers with approximate AI4S simulators speeds up RL for physical control, but surrogate modeling errors can corrupt the learned policy.
AI.method: Using spectral theory and Sobolev estimates, the authors relate AI4S and RL discretization level K to PDE surrogate error and RL lattice approximation error, deriving optimal grid strategies to minimize total cost for a given accuracy and confidence 1 - delta.
AI.result: The theoretical analysis shows that ODE- and PDE-governed environments require distinct allocations of computational effort between physical simulation and RL optimization.
AI.conclusion: The epsilon-N framework provides a principled foundation for designing cost-aware AI4S-RL systems with provable learning guarantees.

title: Multi-Synaptic Cooperation: A Bio-Inspired Framework for Robust and Scalable Continual Learning

AI.tldr: Multi-Synaptic Cooperative Network (MSCN) models cooperative interactions among multiple synapses modulated by local activity, improving continual learning accuracy and robustness to task order.
AI.motivation: Continual learning methods with fixed capacity struggle with catastrophic forgetting on long task sequences and exhibit sensitivity to task ordering.
AI.method: Inspired by biological nervous systems, MSCN uses multi-synaptic connections modulated by local synaptic activity to dynamically activate task-relevant synapses and suppress irrelevant ones during learning.
AI.result: Across four benchmark datasets on both spiking and non-spiking neural networks, MSCN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art continual learning methods with much higher robustness to task-order variation, while revealing an optimal trade-off between synaptic richness and circuit efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Bio-inspired multi-synaptic cooperation offers a scalable, task-order-robust mechanism for continual learning.

title: EA3D: Event-Augmented 3D Diffusion for Generalizable Novel View Synthesis

AI.tldr: EA3D is an event-augmented 3D diffusion framework for generalizable novel view synthesis from event streams and sparse RGB inputs, supported by the new Event-DL3DV dataset.
AI.motivation: Generalizable novel view synthesis from RGB alone struggles under rapid camera motion, whereas existing event-based methods require per-scene optimization that limits scalability.
AI.method: EA3D introduces an EA-Renderer that fuses RGB appearance cues with geometric structure from adaptively sliced event voxels into view-dependent 3D features, which condition a 3D-informed diffusion model; the authors also curate Event-DL3DV pairing synthetic events with multi-view RGB and depth.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on both real-world and synthetic event data show EA3D consistently outperforms optimization-based and generalizable baselines in fidelity and cross-scene generalization.
AI.conclusion: Fusing asynchronous event voxels with sparse RGB in a 3D diffusion framework enables scalable, motion-robust novel view synthesis.

title: VisualPRM400K: An Effective Dataset for Training Multimodal Process Reward Models

AI.tldr: The authors release VisualPRM400K, VisualPRM, and VisualProcessBench, showing that multimodal process reward modeling improves Best-of-N reasoning across MLLMs, including a 5.9-point gain on InternVL2.5-78B.
AI.motivation: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) need reliable step-level verification to improve complex reasoning, yet large-scale multimodal process supervision datasets and benchmarks are lacking.
AI.method: The authors construct VisualPRM400K (~400K multimodal process supervision examples), train VisualPRM to score individual reasoning steps, and build VisualProcessBench to evaluate step-error detection.
AI.result: Under Best-of-N evaluation, VisualPRM improves reasoning across three MLLM types and four model scales, boosting InternVL2.5-78B by 5.9 points across seven multimodal reasoning benchmarks and outperforming Outcome Reward Models and Self-Consistency.
AI.conclusion: Multimodal process reward models trained on large-scale step supervision substantially enhance test-time reasoning in MLLMs.

title: A Near-Optimal Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithm for Federated Bandits

AI.tldr: FedFTRL is a federated multi-armed bandit algorithm for heterogeneous agents that achieves near-optimal regret in both stochastic and adversarial environments, including O(T^(1/2)) adversarial regret.
AI.motivation: In heterogeneous federated multi-armed bandits, no single agent can identify the globally best arm from locally biased observations, and prior adversarial algorithms only achieved O(T^(2/3)) regret.
AI.method: The authors propose FedFTRL to coordinate heterogeneous agents over a communication network without assuming identical local reward distributions.
AI.result: FedFTRL is the first algorithm to achieve near-optimal regret in both stochastic and adversarial regimes—improving adversarial regret to O(T^(1/2))—and demonstrates effectiveness over baselines on synthetic and real-world datasets.
AI.conclusion: FedFTRL establishes near-optimal best-of-both-worlds guarantees for heterogeneous federated bandit learning.

title: VeriRole: Verifiable Role-Awareness through Hint-Guided Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: VeriRole enhances role-awareness in Role-Playing Conversational Agents (RPCAs) using a hint-guided reasoning process and a Verifiable Role-Awareness Reward (VRAR), improving scores on RAIDEN and CharacterEval.
AI.motivation: Maintaining role-awareness in RPCAs is challenging because the creative nature of role-playing makes it difficult to design verifiable reward signals for reinforcement learning.
AI.method: VeriRole introduces a hint mechanism that extracts deterministic cues from the context before main response generation, and uses these hints to compute a Verifiable Role-Awareness Reward (VRAR) for RL optimization.
AI.result: A Qwen2.5-32B model optimized with VeriRole achieves an 18.9% increase in average score on RAIDEN and a 4.55% increase on CharacterEval.
AI.conclusion: VeriRole effectively quantifies and improves role-awareness in RPCAs, yielding superior persona consistency and robustness.

title: Taming Hierarchical Image Coding Optimization: A Spectral Regularization Perspective

AI.tldr: This paper proposes training-only intra-scale and inter-scale spectral regularization schemes for hierarchical learned image compression, accelerating training and improving rate-distortion performance over VTM-22.0.
AI.motivation: Existing hierarchical image coding methods suffer from cross-scale energy dispersion and spectral aliasing during training, which limits optimization efficiency and practical performance.
AI.method: The authors introduce intra-scale frequency regularization to encourage a smooth low-to-high frequency buildup across scales and inter-scale similarity regularization to suppress cross-scale spectral aliasing, applied only during training with zero inference overhead.
AI.result: The method accelerates vanilla model training by 2.3x, achieves an average 20.65% rate-distortion gain over VTM-22.0 on public datasets, and outperforms existing single-scale approaches.
AI.conclusion: Explicit spectral regularization resolves optimization bottlenecks in hierarchical image coding and sets a new state of the art in learned image compression.

title: Fed-Duet: Dual Expert-Orchestrated Framework for Continual Federated Vision-Language Learning

AI.tldr: Fed-Duet is a dual expert-orchestrated framework for continual federated vision-language learning that fuses server-coordinated semantic prompts with client-personalized modular adapters via cross-attention.
AI.motivation: Existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods fail under continual federated learning with evolving non-IID tasks, while traditional federated continual learning methods struggle to preserve cross-modal alignment in vision-language models.
AI.method: Fed-Duet combines server-coordinated semantic prompts and client-personalized modular adapters, dynamically fusing both pathways through a cross-attention mechanism to transfer knowledge while mitigating forgetting.
AI.result: Evaluated across multiple continual learning tasks in federated vision-language settings, Fed-Duet achieves superior performance and stability compared to existing approaches.
AI.conclusion: Coordinated expert composition enables scalable and robust multimodal continual learning in federated settings.

title: Leveraging Pretrained Knowledge at Inference Time: LoRA-Gated Contrastive Decoding for Multilingual Factual Language Generation in Adapted LLMs

AI.tldr: LoRA-Gated Contrastive Decoding (LGCD) is a training-free inference-time framework that reduces hallucinations and improves factuality in language-adapted LLMs by referencing approximated pretrained knowledge.
AI.motivation: LLMs adapted to specific languages via continual pretraining or instruction tuning suffer from catastrophic forgetting of general world knowledge, causing factual inaccuracies in multilingual settings.
AI.method: LGCD extracts factual representations from FFN layers via LoRA-based decomposition to approximate pretrained knowledge, dynamically gates decoding using token-level confidence, and applies contrastive decoding with Top-K masking to revise uncertain predictions.
AI.result: Across multilingual multiple-choice and long-form QA tasks in nine languages, LGCD effectively mitigates hallucinations and enhances factual accuracy without extra training or access to pretraining data.
AI.conclusion: Pretrained knowledge can be strategically reintroduced at inference time to promote factual multilingual generation in adapted LLMs.

title: Hyden: A Hybrid Dual-Path Encoder for Monocular Geometry of High-resolution Images

AI.tldr: Hyden is a hybrid dual-path vision encoder with self-distillation for high-resolution monocular depth, point map, and surface normal estimation, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy at low inference latency.
AI.motivation: High-resolution monocular geometry estimation faces high inference costs with standard transformers and a scarcity of high-quality high-resolution supervision.
AI.method: Hyden pairs a fixed-resolution Vision Transformer branch for global context with a full-resolution CNN branch for fine details fused via a lightweight MLP, and uses a self-distillation framework generating pseudo-labels from both low-resolution full images and high-resolution crops.
AI.result: Integrated into DepthAnything-v2 and MoGe2, Hyden achieves state-of-the-art results on high-resolution benchmarks with the lowest inference latency among competing methods.
AI.conclusion: Combining dual-path global-local encoding with multi-scale self-distillation enables fast, accurate monocular geometry estimation on multi-megapixel images.

title: Calibrated Information Bottleneck for Trusted Multi-modal Clustering

AI.tldr: Calibrated Information Bottleneck (CLIB) is a multi-modal clustering framework using a parallel multi-head architecture and dynamic pseudo-label selection to achieve accurate and well-calibrated clustering.
AI.motivation: Existing Information Bottleneck (IB) multi-modal clustering methods suffer from noisy pseudo-labels and biased Mutual Information (MI) estimation, leading to unstable training and overconfident clustering outcomes.
AI.method: CLIB employs a parallel multi-head network with one primary cluster head and modality-specific calibration heads to correct MI estimation distortion, alongside an information-redundancy-based dynamic pseudo-label selection strategy.
AI.result: Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that CLIB achieves competitive clustering accuracy and strong performance on the expected calibration error metric.
AI.conclusion: Calibrating IB with modality-specific heads and dynamic pseudo-label selection yields both accurate and trustworthy multi-modal clustering.

title: PALC: Preference Alignment via Logit Calibration

AI.tldr: PALC is a parameter-efficient test-time alignment framework that calibrates LLM logits directly in vocabulary space using a bottleneck architecture, outperforming most test-time alignment methods at near-baseline speed.
AI.motivation: Aligning LLMs with human preferences typically requires expensive training, complex reward models, or representation engineering that suffers from hidden-state superposition and decoding overhead.
AI.method: PALC uses a bottleneck architecture to compress hidden states and generate position-dependent calibration vectors in vocabulary space, with a single scaling factor to adjust alignment strength at runtime without retraining.
AI.result: Experiments show PALC outperforms most test-time alignment methods while maintaining near-baseline inference speed, and ablations confirm that human preferences concentrate on low-dimensional manifolds.
AI.conclusion: Vocabulary-space logit calibration provides an interpretable, fast, and scalable paradigm for preference alignment in resource-constrained deployments.

title: ContextIF: Enhancing Instruction-Following through Context Reward

AI.tldr: ContextIF is an RL framework using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a context reward to automatically generate constraint summaries and demonstrations that improve LLM instruction-following.
AI.motivation: Supervised fine-tuning and preference learning struggle to generalize to novel instructions and can harm general capabilities, while in-context learning relies heavily on manually curated demonstration pools.
AI.method: ContextIF trains a context generator via GRPO guided by a context reward to produce precise constraint summaries and optimal demonstrations tailored to input instructions without modifying target LLM parameters.
AI.result: Evaluated on multiple instruction-following benchmarks with open-source LLMs, ContextIF substantially outperforms existing SFT and ICL methods, generalizes to unseen constraints, and preserves target model capabilities.
AI.conclusion: Automated RL-based context generation offers a scalable and adaptable way to enhance instruction-following without altering target model weights.

title: Structured Reasoning for LLMs: A Unified Framework for Efficiency and Explainability

AI.tldr: Structured Reasoning models LLM reasoning as a sparse directed acyclic graph using structured step tags, MaxFlow reward, and LCS reward, outperforming GRPO on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models.
AI.motivation: LLMs struggle with complex reasoning tasks such as logical deduction and planning because they rely primarily on token-level probability relationships rather than step-level structure.
AI.method: The framework collects domain-agnostic reasoning step tags to build a structured dataset, represents reasoning as a directed acyclic graph, and optimizes it with a MaxFlow reward for single-graph sparsity and an LCS reward for multi-graph consistency.
AI.result: On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and 7B, Structured Reasoning consistently outperforms GRPO and tuned baselines across 0.5k-8k context lengths, showing higher efficiency with fewer steps and stability across temperatures 0.1 to 1.0.
AI.conclusion: Step-level graph formulation with flow and subsequence rewards improves both the efficiency and explainability of LLM reasoning.

title: Group-Normalized Implicit Value Optimization for Language Models

AI.tldr: Group-Normalized Implicit Value Optimization (GN-IVO) is a critic-free RL algorithm for LLMs that learns step-level values implicitly via a group-normalized distributional matching objective.
AI.motivation: RL fine-tuning of LLMs suffers from fine-grained credit assignment under sparse sequence-level rewards, while explicit critic networks add computational overhead and training instability.
AI.method: GN-IVO learns step-level values implicitly from the policy using a group-normalized distributional matching objective across sampled responses, avoiding both an explicit critic and intractable partition function computation.
AI.result: Theoretically, GN-IVO recovers the true value function up to a constant and preserves the optimal policy; empirically, it consistently outperforms strong RL baselines across diverse text generation and reasoning tasks.
AI.conclusion: Group-normalized implicit value learning provides a stable, critic-free alternative for fine-grained credit assignment in LLM RL.

title: CoLA: Co-Calibrated Logit Adjustment for Long-Tailed Semi-Supervised Learning

AI.tldr: CoLA is a long-tailed semi-supervised learning framework that co-designs class-wise effective sample size estimation and meta-learned overall logit adjustment strength, outperforming baselines on four benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing dynamic Logit Adjustment (LA) methods for long-tailed semi-supervised learning overestimate head classes due to sample redundancy and treat overall adjustment strength as a fixed hyperparameter despite its sensitivity to distribution estimates.
AI.method: CoLA estimates each class's effective sample size via the effective rank of its representations for class-wise adjustment, and formulates overall adjustment strength as a learnable parameter optimized via meta-learning on a refined proxy validation set.
AI.result: Supported by a theoretical generalization bound, CoLA outperforms existing baselines across four public benchmarks under standard long-tail setups.
AI.conclusion: Jointly calibrating class-wise effective sample size and learnable adjustment strength mitigates confirmation bias in long-tailed semi-supervised learning.

title: Heterogeneous Agent Q-weighted Policy Optimization

AI.tldr: Heterogeneous Agent Q-weighted Policy Optimization (HAQO) unifies sequential advantage-aware updates, Q-weighted variational surrogates, and entropy regularization to achieve stable and expressive multi-agent RL.
AI.motivation: Multi-agent reinforcement learning faces a tension between stability (which existing methods achieve via restrictive unimodal policies) and expressiveness (which generative models offer without optimization guarantees).
AI.method: HAQO combines sequential advantage-aware updates, Q-weighted variational surrogates, and entropy regularization, extending trust-region theory to diffusion-based policies with intractable log-likelihoods.
AI.result: HAQO achieves superior returns and reduced variance compared to policy-gradient baselines across diverse benchmarks, with ablations confirming the roles of sequential updates, expressive policies, and entropy regularization.
AI.conclusion: HAQO reconciles stability and multimodal expressiveness in heterogeneous MARL with monotone improvement guarantees.

title: Towards All-Atom Foundation Models for Biomolecular Binding Affinity Prediction

AI.tldr: Atom-level Diffusion Transformer (ADiT) repurposes AlphaFold 3 for representation learning to predict biomolecular binding affinity across diverse interaction types without MSA or template dependencies.
AI.motivation: Predicting biomolecular binding affinity is hindered by limited high-quality data and the narrow specialization of existing methods to single interaction types.
AI.method: ADiT shifts from generative structure prediction to encoding observed geometry using unified sequence-structure tokenization, a simplified trunk, and diffusion transformers pretrained on PDB with a denoising objective, without MSAs or templates.
AI.result: Pretrained ADiT variants achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance across protein-ligand, drug-target, protein-protein, and antibody-antigen benchmarks, scale with model size, and identify wet-lab validated affinity-enhancing antibody mutations.
AI.conclusion: ADiT establishes a generalizable all-atom foundation model framework for biomolecular binding affinity prediction.

title: Masked Skill Token Training for Hierarchical Off-Dynamics Transfer

AI.tldr: Masked Skill Token Training (MSTT) is an offline hierarchical RL framework that uses unsupervised trajectory tokenization and masked Bellman updates to transfer policies across off-dynamics environments from observation-only demonstrations.
AI.motivation: Generalizing policies across environments with altered dynamics in offline RL is difficult when direct interaction, fine-tuning, or action labels are unavailable.
AI.method: MSTT builds a discrete skill space via unsupervised trajectory tokenization, trains a skill-conditioned value function with masked Bellman updates that selectively disable skills to simulate dynamics shifts, and executes actions via a diffusion trajectory generator with feasibility filtering.
AI.result: Experiments in both discrete and continuous domains demonstrate that mask-guided planning enables robust generalization under dynamics shifts without action labels or target environment access.
AI.conclusion: Skill-level masking provides a scalable, structure-aware mechanism for offline off-dynamics policy transfer.

title: Naming to Learn: Class Incremental Learning for Vision-Language Model with Unlabeled Data

AI.tldr: N2L is a recursive class incremental learning method for vision-language models using only unlabeled data and class names, refining pseudo labels via dimensionality reduction and bi-level weight adjustment.
AI.motivation: Class incremental learning (CIL) typically assumes fully labeled data for new tasks, whereas using noisy VLM pseudo labels on unlabeled data aggravates catastrophic forgetting.
AI.method: N2L uses a recursive MSE regression objective, refines pseudo labels iteratively using a classifier on dimensionality-reduced image features, and applies bi-level weight adjustment for intra-class confidence and inter-class balance.
AI.result: Theoretical analysis supports the pseudo-label refinement, and experiments across multiple datasets show N2L outperforms state-of-the-art methods while matching joint training with unlabeled data.
AI.conclusion: Recursive regression with feature-reduced label refinement and bi-level weighting effectively mitigates forgetting in unlabeled VLM class incremental learning.

title: FlowSearcher: Synthesizing Memory-Guided Agentic Workflows for Web Information Seeking

AI.tldr: FlowSearcher formulates web information seeking as memory-guided agentic workflow synthesis, matching or exceeding RLHF-trained web agents on GAIA, BrowseComp, and GPQA without training.
AI.motivation: Existing deep research agents rely on rigid, linear ReAct-style tool chains that struggle to adapt to diverse query types and tool-use strategies.
AI.method: FlowSearcher decomposes queries into subgoals, synthesizes a tailored workflow graph per subgoal with dynamic tool depth and ordering, and uses a hierarchical memory of past workflows to guide orchestration and execution without supervised training or RLHF.
AI.result: On GAIA, BrowseComp, and GPQA, FlowSearcher consistently matches or exceeds RLHF-trained web agents under the same model backbone.
AI.conclusion: Experience-conditioned workflow synthesis enables flexible multi-path web exploration and reuse without additional model training.

title: High Probability Bounds for Non-Convex Stochastic Optimization with Momentum

AI.tldr: This paper establishes high-probability convergence and generalization bounds for non-convex stochastic gradient descent with momentum (SGDM), including faster rates under Polyak-Lojasiewicz and Bernstein conditions.
AI.motivation: Despite SGDM's widespread use in machine learning, high-probability convergence and generalization bounds for SGDM in non-convex settings remain scarce.
AI.method: The authors derive high-probability bounds on the gradient norm for general non-convex SGDM, function-value error bounds under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, and sharper bounds under an additional mild Bernstein condition on the gradient.
AI.result: The general non-convex convergence bounds are tighter than prior results, the generalization bounds are the first for SGDM, and the Bernstein condition yields learning rates up to O_tilde(1/n^2) in the low-noise regime.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a systematic theoretical characterization of high-probability learning guarantees for non-convex SGDM.

title: Quantized Gradient Projection for Memory-Efficient Continual Learning

AI.tldr: Quantized Gradient Projection Memory (QGPM) compresses and preserves past gradient subspaces for continual learning, achieving state-of-the-art performance under fixed memory budgets.
AI.motivation: Continual learning in real-world deployments requires preserving prior knowledge from non-stationary data in a memory-efficient and privacy-preserving manner.
AI.method: QGPM combines distribution-aware basis-wise quantization, Quantization Error-Aware (QEA) gradient projection that relaxes orthogonality to counter quantization drift, and on-the-fly sparse sketching for runtime efficiency.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple benchmarks show that QGPM achieves state-of-the-art performance under fixed memory budgets.
AI.conclusion: Quantized subspace compression with error-aware projection enables scalable, privacy-preserving continual learning.

title: Bayesian Ensemble for Sequential Decision-Making

AI.tldr: Bayesian Ensemble (BE) adds a lightweight Bayesian bandit layer over ensemble members to dynamically update member sampling distributions from observed rewards, improving sequential decision-making.
AI.motivation: Standard ensemble methods for uncertainty modeling sample members from a fixed uniform distribution, ignoring observed reward feedback in sequential decision-making.
AI.method: BE treats ensemble member selection as a bandit problem, updating the sampling distribution over members via Bayesian inference on observed rewards, instantiated as Bayesian Ensemble Bandit and Bayesian Ensemble Deep Q-Network.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world bandit and reinforcement learning environments demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of BE.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic Bayesian selection over ensemble members provides a principled improvement over uniform sampling for sequential decision-making.

title: RD-HRL: Generating Reliable Sub-Goals for Long-Horizon Sparse-Reward Tasks

AI.tldr: Reliability-Driven HRL (RD-HRL) introduces a reliability-driven decision mechanism to generate noise-immune sub-goals for long-horizon sparse-reward offline RL, outperforming baselines across multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Hierarchical offline RL methods rely on value functions that suffer from generalization noise, which misguides sub-goal selection in long-horizon sparse-reward tasks.
AI.method: RD-HRL introduces a reliability-driven decision mechanism that provides decision-level targets for the high-level policy, creating a noise-immune decision space to ensure reliable action-level sub-goals.
AI.result: Comprehensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that RD-HRL consistently outperforms baseline methods.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling sub-goal selection from noisy value estimation via reliability-driven decision spaces improves offline hierarchical RL on sparse-reward tasks.

title: ReSplat: Degradation-agnostic Feed-forward Gaussian Splatting via Self-guided Residual Diffusion

AI.tldr: ReSplat is a degradation-agnostic feed-forward Gaussian Splatting framework that jointly estimates restored images and 3D Gaussians via self-guided residual diffusion for robust novel view synthesis.
AI.motivation: Existing novel view synthesis (NVS) methods assume clear inputs or handle only narrow degradation types, limiting their use under real-world blur, low-light, haze, rain, and snow.
AI.method: ReSplat jointly estimates restored images and 3D Gaussians without prior knowledge of degradation types, using the 3D Gaussians generated during diffusion sampling as self-guidance for multi-view consistent image restoration.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that ReSplat significantly outperforms existing methods across blur, low-light, haze, rain, and snow conditions.
AI.conclusion: Self-guided 3D Gaussian residual diffusion enables generalizable, degradation-agnostic feed-forward NVS.

title: TrajTok: What makes for a good trajectory tokenizer in behavior generation?

AI.tldr: TrajTok combines rule-based vocabulary setup with data-driven filtering and spatial-aware label smoothing for autonomous driving trajectory tokenization, winning first place in the 2025 Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge.
AI.motivation: Data-driven trajectory tokenizers have good utilization but poor coverage and noise sensitivity, whereas rule-based tokenizers have good coverage but many useless tokens.
AI.method: TrajTok analyzes vocabulary coverage, utilization, symmetry, and robustness, combining rule-based candidate setup with data-driven filtering and selection, alongside spatial-aware label smoothing for cross-entropy loss.
AI.result: TrajTok achieves balanced coverage, utilization, symmetry, and robustness, and wins first place in the 2025 Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid rule-based and data-driven tokenization with spatial-aware smoothing provides an effective discrete representation for autonomous driving behavior generation.

title: Parameter-Efficient Reinforcement Learning using Prefix Optimization

AI.tldr: Optimizing only the first k tokens (e.g., k=32) via Prefix Clustering or Prefix-RL significantly improves math reasoning accuracy at a tiny fraction of standard RLVR compute.
AI.motivation: It is unclear whether Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) creates new reasoning capabilities or mainly steers models toward answer formats already in the reference distribution.
AI.method: The authors optimize only the first k tokens of each solution while sampling the rest from the reference model, comparing Prefix Clustering and Prefix-RL (finetuning a lightweight adapter with RL).
AI.result: Tuning only the first k tokens yields substantial math accuracy improvements across different models and benchmarks at a tiny fraction of standard RL compute, robust across prefix lengths and seeds.
AI.conclusion: Prefix optimization offers a compute-efficient alternative to full RLVR and suggests that RL gains partly stem from upweighting preferable solution strategies.

title: RoRE: Rotary Ray Embedding for Generalised Multi-Modal Scene Understanding

AI.tldr: Rotary Ray Embedding (RoRE) embeds image patches directly as rays using a learned rotary positional embedding (RoPE), improving generalization across perspective, fisheye, and RGB-thermal scene understanding.
AI.motivation: Feedforward implicit rendering transformers struggle to inject camera parameters in a way that generalizes across unconventional camera geometries and multi-modal sensing setups.
AI.method: RoRE embeds image patches directly as rays using a learning-based rotary positional embedding, allowing a single network to integrate arbitrary numbers of cameras and modalities.
AI.result: Evaluated on perspective imagery, fisheye cameras, and multi-modal RGB-thermal setups, RoRE demonstrates improved generalization and cross-modal consistency over existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Relative ray-based rotary embeddings enable adaptable, plug-and-play multi-modal vision systems across diverse camera geometries.

title: PCLR: Progressively Compressed LoRA for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

AI.tldr: Progressively Compressed LoRA (PCLR) uses a Compression-Integration-Learning pipeline and a LoRA Rank Pool to reduce forgetting and memory overhead in multimodal continual instruction tuning.
AI.motivation: Continual instruction tuning of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) suffers from catastrophic forgetting, while model-extension methods that add new branches incur excessive memory consumption.
AI.method: PCLR decomposes LoRA into rank vectors in a LoRA Rank Pool (LRP) and applies a progressive Compression-Integration-Learning (CIL) pipeline that compresses old parameters, merges similar task knowledge, and reallocates capacity for new tasks.
AI.result: On LLaVA-7B, CIL reduces forgetting from 11.29 to 5.09 and progressive learning further reduces it to 3.39; PCLR outperforms extension methods while keeping memory close to non-extension methods.
AI.conclusion: Fine-grained rank-pool compression and progressive consolidation resolve the trade-off between forgetting and memory explosion in multimodal continual learning.

title: Automata Learning and Identification of the Support of Language Models

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes DFA learnability in the Next Symbol Prediction (NSP) setting and introduces L*_nsp, an extension of Angluin's L* algorithm that extracts DFAs from Transformer language models.
AI.motivation: While NSP supervision has been used empirically to analyze neural sequence models, its formal learnability properties and utility for identifying the support of language models were not established.
AI.method: The authors prove identifiability of n-state DFAs from positive examples with NSP labels, show PAC-learning and membership-only exact identification remain hard, and propose L*_nsp using an LM-based teacher for membership queries and prefix-conditioned generation.
AI.result: Experiments on 11 regular languages show L*_nsp successfully extracts DFAs from Transformer language models and identifies erroneous examples.
AI.conclusion: L*_nsp provides a formal and practical framework for extracting and auditing the regular-language support learned by Transformer LMs.

title: Bayesian Robust Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Against Unknown Adversaries

AI.tldr: BATPAL models deployment-time adversarial attacks in cooperative MARL as a Bayesian Dec-POMDP game with a continuum of adversary types and computes robust policies via simultaneous gradient updates, outperforming baselines.
AI.motivation: Cooperative MARL agents deployed in practice can face adversaries with unknown attack objectives, creating uncertainty that standard robust MARL methods do not address.
AI.method: BATPAL formulates a Bayesian Dec-POMDP with a continuum of adversarial types, partitions adversarial policies against a reference policy to form a finite-type Bayesian game, solves an externally constrained RL problem with provable convergence, and applies simultaneous gradient updates for a perfect Bayesian equilibrium.
AI.result: Experiments across diverse benchmarks show BATPAL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines under a wide variety of attack strategies.
AI.conclusion: Partitioning continuous adversary types into a finite Bayesian game enables provably convergent, adaptive defense in cooperative MARL.

title: SAM-Veteran: An MLLM-Based Human-like SAM Agent for Reasoning Segmentation

AI.tldr: SAM-Veteran is an MLLM-based agent trained with GRPO and dynamic sampling to interactively control SAM through bounding boxes, refinement points, and adaptive termination, setting new state of the art in reasoning segmentation.
AI.motivation: Existing MLLM+SAM reasoning segmentation paradigms fail to exploit SAM's iterative interactive mask refinement capability.
AI.method: SAM-Veteran trains an MLLM with multi-task GRPO and a dynamic box-and-point sampling strategy to generate initial bounding boxes, propose point refinements from intermediate SAM masks, and adaptively terminate.
AI.result: Across diverse in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, SAM-Veteran achieves human-like interactive segmentation and establishes new state-of-the-art performance.
AI.conclusion: Multi-task RL over iterative box-and-point interactions unlocks SAM's full refinement potential for reasoning segmentation.

title: Compositional Generalization through Gradient Search in Nonparametric Latent Space

AI.tldr: Abduction Transformer uses a nonparametric mixture latent space with information-theoretic regularization and test-time gradient search to achieve strong compositional generalization on meta-learning tasks.
AI.motivation: Standard deep learning architectures fail at systematic reasoning requiring compositional generalization across novel recombinations of learned knowledge.
AI.method: Abduction Transformer represents inferred hidden causes of few-shot instances as nonparametric mixture distributions and refines them at test time via gradient-based variational posterior inference.
AI.result: The model outperforms standard transformers and a contemporary test-time adaptive variational approach on program induction, Raven's progressive matrices, and linguistic systematicity tasks.
AI.conclusion: Test-time gradient search in a regularized nonparametric latent space offers a promising mechanism for systematic compositional generalization.

title: From Pixels to Semantics: Unified Facial Action Representation Learning for Micro-Expression Analysis

AI.tldr: D-FACE pretrains a discrete facial action tokenizer and combines a sparse-attention Transformer with emotion-description-guided CLIP (EDCLIP) alignment for state-of-the-art micro-expression recognition and generation.
AI.motivation: Micro-expression recognition (MER) methods relying on pixel-level optical flow or frame differences are identity-sensitive and generalize poorly under scarce annotations.
AI.method: D-FACE pretrains an identity- and domain-invariant discrete facial action tokenizer on large-scale facial videos, models action sequences with a sparse-attention pooling Transformer, and aligns tokens with textual emotion anchors via EDCLIP while keeping the ambiguous "others" class distant.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple datasets show D-FACE achieves state-of-the-art recognition accuracy and high-quality cross-identity and cross-domain micro-expression generation.
AI.conclusion: Shifting from pixel-level motion descriptors to discrete semantic facial action tokens enables generalizable micro-expression analysis.

title: VibeVoice: Expressive Podcast Generation with Next-Token Diffusion

AI.tldr: VibeVoice is a zero-shot next-token diffusion TTS model using 7.5 Hz continuous speech tokenizers to synthesize up to 30 minutes of expressive multi-speaker podcast audio with up to 4 speakers.
AI.motivation: Traditional TTS systems struggle with scalability, speaker consistency, and natural turn-taking in long-form multi-speaker conversational audio.
AI.method: VibeVoice employs continuous speech tokenizers at an ultra-low 7.5 Hz frame rate, an annotation pipeline generating pseudo transcriptions and turn-taking labels for podcast data, and a next-token diffusion framework.
AI.result: VibeVoice synthesizes up to 30 minutes of speech with up to 4 speakers (surpassing typical 1-2 speaker limits) with natural turn-taking, pacing, and non-lexical cues such as breaths and lip smacks.
AI.conclusion: Ultra-low-frame-rate continuous tokenization paired with next-token diffusion enables scalable, expressive long-form multi-speaker speech synthesis.

title: Permutation-Consistent Variational Encoding for Incomplete Multi-View Multi-Label Classification

AI.tldr: Permutation-Consistent Variational Encoding (PCVE) combines an information bottleneck, permutation-consistent regularization, and a masked multi-label objective for incomplete multi-view multi-label classification, outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Incomplete multi-view multi-label learning requires integrating information under simultaneous view and label incompleteness without view-private redundancy or explicit imputation.
