AI.method: PCVE maximizes a variational evidence lower bound with an information bottleneck, applies permutation-consistent regularization to align distributions of shared semantics across views, and uses a masked multi-label objective to model label dependencies from available supervision.
AI.result: Experiments across diverse benchmarks and missing ratios show consistent gains over state-of-the-art methods and reliable inference of missing views without explicit imputation.
AI.conclusion: Permutation-consistent variational alignment provides a general, imputation-free solution for incomplete multi-view multi-label classification.

title: MoCa: Modeling Object Consistency for 3D Camera Control in Video Generation

AI.tldr: MoCa is a dual-branch video generation framework that models object view, appearance, and motion consistency to achieve accurate 3D camera control without explicit 3D supervision.
AI.motivation: Existing camera-controllable text-to-video methods either produce artifacts when conditioning directly in 2D pixel space or generalize poorly when relying on explicit 3D supervision.
AI.method: MoCa uses a Spatial-Temporal Camera Encoder with Plucker embedding for view consistency, persistent vision-language semantic guidance for appearance consistency, and object-aware motion disentanglement to separate object dynamics from global camera movement.
AI.result: Experiments show MoCa achieves accurate 3D camera control while preserving video quality.
AI.conclusion: Modeling 2D object consistency implicitly bridges the gap between 2D pixel generation and 3D camera geometry.

title: DispViT: Direct Stereo Disparity Regression with a Single-Stream Vision Transformer

AI.tldr: DispViT replaces explicit cost-volume matching with direct stereo disparity regression using a single-stream Vision Transformer and shift-embedding tokenization, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness.
AI.motivation: Matching-centric stereo methods rely on cost volumes and local correspondence refinement, which fail irreversibly under occlusion or non-Lambertian ambiguities.
AI.method: DispViT tokenizes binocular views with an asymmetrically initialized stereo tokenizer and channel-grouped shift embeddings, regresses probability-based disparity directly via a single-stream ViT, and sharpens predictions with a lightweight refinement module.
AI.result: Experiments on standard benchmarks show DispViT achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with strong resilience to matching ambiguities and wide disparity ranges.
AI.conclusion: Holistic single-stream regression offers a streamlined, robust alternative to cost-volume matching for stereo disparity estimation.

title: Flowing Through States: Neural ODE Regularization for Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a neural ODE-based regularization method that aligns RL latent state transitions with environment dynamics, yielding major performance gains on Atari (A2C) and gridworld (PPO).
AI.motivation: Deep RL agents typically leave latent state transitions implicit, causing potential misalignment with how semantic environment states actually evolve.
AI.method: Drawing an analogy between Markov decision process trajectories and ODE flows, the method regularizes latent embeddings to follow consistent neural ODE flows integrated into Actor-Critic algorithms.
AI.result: Integrating neural ODE regularization yields major performance gains across standard Atari benchmarks for A2C and gridworld environments for PPO.
AI.conclusion: Explicit ODE flow regularization aligns latent representation learning with environment dynamics to improve RL performance.

title: Emergent Discrete Controller Modules for Symbolic Planning in Transformers

AI.tldr: Discrete controller modules insert Gumbel-Softmax-selected program primitives and compact register/flag state into Transformers, improving longest-length algorithmic accuracy by 20-40 points with only 5-7% extra FLOPs.
AI.motivation: Transformers struggle with symbolic planning loops, variable updates, and conditional branching, particularly under length extrapolation.
AI.method: The modules insert ASSIGN, ADD, COMPARE, and BRANCH primitives into Transformer blocks via a Gumbel-Softmax selector over a compact state of registers, flags, and optional memory, with proven bounded-step simulation and O(tau + kappa^-1) relaxation error bounds.
AI.result: The augmented Transformer improves longest-length accuracy by 20-40 points on Sorting, Sum-of-List, and BFS, and yields consistent gains on DROP and RobustFill with interpretable operation traces and ~5-7% added FLOPs.
AI.conclusion: Sparse discrete controller modules equip Transformers with interpretable, length-generalizing symbolic execution.

title: PROS: Towards Compute-Efficient RLVR via Rollout Prefix Reuse

AI.tldr: PROS reuses promising prefixes of historical rollouts as Augmented Queries in RLVR training, prioritized by a hierarchical Bayesian pass-rate model, improving training efficiency and accuracy.
AI.motivation: On-policy rollout generation in RLVR is a major compute bottleneck because independent rollouts for the same query share redundant early reasoning steps.
AI.method: PROS appends self-generated partial rollout prefixes to original queries to form Augmented Queries and uses a hierarchical Bayesian model to estimate pass rates and prioritize batches with the highest reward uncertainty.
AI.result: Experiments across diverse settings show PROS consistently improves training efficiency and achieves higher accuracy than strong baselines.
AI.conclusion: Rollout prefix reuse with uncertainty-based batch selection provides a practical path to compute-efficient RLVR.

title: LoC-Decomp: LLM Autoformalization via Logical Concept Decomposition and Iterative Feedback Correction

AI.tldr: LoC-Decomp combines modular formalization templates, divide-conquer-merge semantic self-checking, and Lean 4 compiler feedback to iteratively refine LLM autoformalization, reaching 93.09% on PutnamBench.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM autoformalization methods lack reliable semantic consistency checks against the original mathematical statement and cannot iteratively refine outputs using error feedback.
AI.method: LoC-Decomp uses a structured CoT-like template to decompose and assemble formalizations, a divide-conquer-merge semantic self-checker, and an iterative refinement loop driven by both semantic and Lean 4 syntactic error signals.
AI.result: Experiments on high-school and undergraduate datasets show significantly higher formalization success rates, reaching 93.09% on PutnamBench (an 18 percentage point gain over the previous SOTA SFT model).
AI.conclusion: Combining modular decomposition with dual semantic and compiler feedback substantially improves the reliability of LLM autoformalization.

title: Topology Matters in RTL Circuit Representation Learning

AI.tldr: TopoRTL decomposes RTL circuits into register cones and applies topology-aware positional encodings and cross-modal contrastive alignment, outperforming existing methods on RTL representation learning tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing language-model approaches treat RTL code as plain text, ignoring its inherent structured dataflow graph topology and limiting downstream performance.
AI.method: TopoRTL decomposes RTL designs into register cones with dual behavior-aware modalities, introduces three topology-aware positional encodings for attention, and applies topology-guided cross-modal contrastive alignment.
AI.result: Experiments show TopoRTL significantly outperforms existing methods across multiple downstream RTL tasks such as PPA prediction, circuit generation, and retrieval.
AI.conclusion: Explicit topological modeling is essential for high-quality RTL circuit representation learning.

title: A General Spatio-Temporal Backbone with Scalable Contextual Pattern Bank for Urban Continual Forecasting

AI.tldr: STBP pairs a frozen frequency-domain and linear-graph-attention spatio-temporal backbone with an incrementally expanded contextual pattern bank, outperforming SOTA baselines in urban continual forecasting.
AI.motivation: Existing continual spatio-temporal forecasting methods use limited-capacity backbones and struggle to balance stability against catastrophic forgetting with adaptability to graph expansion and distribution shifts.
AI.method: STBP keeps a general frequency-domain and lightweight linear-graph-attention backbone fixed during incremental training while expanding a contextual pattern bank to capture evolving node-level heterogeneity.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show STBP outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both forecasting accuracy and scalability for continual spatio-temporal forecasting.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling a fixed general spatio-temporal backbone from an expandable pattern bank effectively resolves the stability-adaptability trade-off in urban continual forecasting.

title: Consis-GCPO: Consistency-Preserving Group Causal Preference Optimization for Vision Customization

AI.tldr: Consis-GCPO reformulates multi-modal subject-driven generation as discrete-time causal modeling to assign temporally-weighted advantages to textual and visual conditions across denoising timesteps.
AI.motivation: Existing GRPO-based preference alignment methods apply uniform optimization across all denoising timesteps, ignoring that text guides semantic structure early while visual references anchor details later.
AI.method: The authors introduce decoupled causal intervention trajectories to quantify instantaneous causal effects at each denoising timestep and convert them into temporally-weighted advantages for targeted optimization.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that Consis-GCPO achieves superior subject consistency while preserving strong text-following capabilities, particularly in complex multi-subject scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Modeling the temporal dynamics of conditioning modalities enables more accurate credit assignment and improves personalized visual generation.

title: MARTI: A Framework for Multi-Agent LLM Systems Reinforced Training and Inference

AI.tldr: MARTI is an open-source framework for scalable centralized multi-agent LLM interactions and distributed reinforcement learning training with multi-turn asynchronous rollouts.
AI.motivation: Training multi-agent LLM systems requires scalable infrastructure that supports complex interaction workflows, asynchronous rollouts, and diverse reward signals.
AI.method: MARTI combines centralized multi-agent interactions, distributed policy training, multi-turn asynchronous rollouts, and dynamic workflows integrating both rule-based verifiable rewards and LLM-based generative rewards.
AI.result: Experiments on diverse mathematical tasks show that multi-agent LLM systems trained with MARTI outperform single-agent systems within the same inference budget after convergence.
AI.conclusion: MARTI provides a scalable foundation for advancing collaborative multi-agent LLM reasoning systems.

title: Temporal Graph Thumbnail: Robust Representation Learning with Global Evolutionary Skeleton

AI.tldr: Temporal Graph Thumbnail (TGT) extracts a temporal graph's global evolutionary skeleton using von Neumann graph entropy and node mutual information to improve representation learning robustness.
AI.motivation: Existing temporal graph methods rely on local spatiotemporal neighbor sampling, which struggles with severe noise and long-term dependencies because it neglects global evolutionary regularities.
AI.method: TGT models a global evolutionary skeleton thumbnail via von Neumann graph entropy and node mutual information, then uses this thumbnail to guide representation learning optimization.
AI.result: Theoretical analysis and extensive experiments demonstrate that TGT achieves superior capability and robustness over baselines, especially in rapidly evolving and noisy environments.
AI.conclusion: Capturing global evolutionary regularities through a compact graph thumbnail enhances robustness in temporal graph representation learning.

title: Knowledge Externalization: Reversible Unlearning and Modular Retrieval in Multimodal Large Language Models

AI.tldr: Knowledge Externalization transfers targeted knowledge from MLLM parameters into external memory tokens for reversible unlearning, continuous editing, and compositional retrieval.
AI.motivation: Existing machine unlearning methods irreversibly alter model parameters to erase sensitive data, conflicting with privacy regulations that require auditable, reversible, and user-controllable data management.
AI.method: The framework uses Dual-Stream Memory Tuning to move targeted knowledge into external memory tokens and Soft Orthogonal Weighting to prevent gradient interference across multiple externalized concepts.
AI.result: The method effectively forgets target concepts in the base model, restores them via memory tokens, supports dynamic post-externalization editing, and enables compositional combination of multiple tokens.
AI.conclusion: Externalizing knowledge into modular memory tokens enables reversible, editable, and privacy-compliant knowledge management in MLLMs.

title: Prompt-Robust Vision-Language Models via Meta-Finetuning

AI.tldr: Promise is a dual-loop meta-finetuning framework that reduces prompt sensitivity in vision-language models and improves generalization across unseen prompt formulations.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models exhibit unstable performance under natural language prompt variations, hindering reliable real-world deployment.
AI.method: Promise adapts token embeddings in an inner loop over varied prompts and optimizes outer-loop generalization on unseen prompts, using adaptive prompt weighting and token-specific learning rates.
AI.result: Theoretical analysis proves one-step outer risk reduction and tighter generalization bounds, and experiments across 15 benchmarks show reduced prompt sensitivity and improved stability over existing prompt learning methods.
AI.conclusion: Meta-finetuning with adaptive prompt weighting and token-specific learning rates provides provable and practical prompt robustness for VLMs.

title: HiPO: Self-Hint Policy Optimization for RLVR

AI.tldr: HiPO (Hint-guided Policy Optimization) repurposes initial steps of rare successful trajectories as on-policy hints to overcome sparse rewards in RLVR for long-horizon reasoning.
AI.motivation: Current RLVR methods suffer from the near-miss problem, where sparse rewards nullify learning signals for almost-correct attempts, leading to exploration stagnation.
AI.method: HiPO captures occasional successful trajectories within a training batch and reuses their initial correct steps as on-policy hints to create a dense contrastive learning signal.
AI.result: Across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, HiPO improves average avg@32 by +5.0 percentage points over GRPO, including +10.3 pp on CMIMC 2025, +4.9 pp on BRUMO 2025, +4.6 pp on AIME 2024, and +3.1 pp on AIME 2025.
AI.conclusion: Repurposing rare successes into on-policy hints provides an efficient and scalable exploration paradigm for autonomous long-horizon reasoning.

title: GOLDILOCS: GENERAL OBJECT-LEVEL DETECTION AND LABELING OF CHANGES IN SCENES

AI.tldr: GOLDILOCS is a zero-shot, pose-agnostic method for object-level semantic scene change detection that reformulates the task as 3D reconstruction over time.
AI.motivation: Supervised scene change detection methods fail to generalize out-of-domain, while existing zero-shot methods ignore 3D geometry and 3D-centric methods require multi-view inputs rather than image pairs.
AI.method: GOLDILOCS uses dense stereo reconstruction to estimate camera poses and build a commonality pointmap by filtering geometric inconsistencies, then detects rigid changes via mask tracking and nonrigid changes via SSIM heatmaps.
AI.result: Evaluations across pairwise and multi-view datasets in binary and multi-class settings show GOLDILOCS outperforms prior methods, including supervised baselines.
AI.conclusion: Reformulating scene change detection as 3D reconstruction over time enables robust, pose-agnostic change detection in the wild.

title: Optimal Robust Subsidy Policies for Irrational Agent in Principal-Agent MDPs

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes robust subsidy policies in principal-agent MDPs when the agent exhibits bounded rationality under global and state-wise epsilon-incentive-compatibility.
AI.motivation: Standard principal-agent models assume perfectly rational agents, whereas real agents may deviate from optimal policies after receiving subsidies.
AI.method: The authors prove that under global epsilon-incentive-compatibility, finding the optimal robust subsidy reduces to a one-dimensional concave optimization problem, and they analyze two state-wise definitions.
AI.result: Optimal subsidies under global bounded rationality concentrate along social-welfare-maximizing trajectories with bounded welfare loss, whereas state-wise definitions lead to either non-Markovian policies or NP-hard optimization.
AI.conclusion: Global bounded rationality yields tractable robust subsidy design, while state-wise incentive-compatibility introduces fundamental computational intractability.

title: Consistent Noisy Latent Rewards for Trajectory Preference Optimization in Diffusion Models

AI.tldr: This paper introduces SLRM and TAPO to enable noise-compatible reward estimation on noisy latents and consistent multi-timestep trajectory preference optimization in diffusion models.
AI.motivation: Existing reward-model-based diffusion alignment suffers from unreliable reward estimation on noisy latents and inconsistent preference rankings when evaluating only a single timestep.
AI.method: SLRM uses the full diffusion model with learnable task tokens and score-function augmentation for noisy latent evaluation, while TAPO performs SDE sampling and reward evaluation across multiple timesteps.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on Text-to-Image and Text-to-Video generation tasks show significant improvements in noisy latent evaluation and human preference alignment.
AI.conclusion: Combining score-enhanced latent reward modeling with multi-timestep trajectory evaluation improves preference alignment for diffusion models.

title: Cross-Domain Lossy Compression via Rate- and Classification-Constrained Optimal Transport

AI.tldr: This paper formulates cross-domain lossy compression as rate- and classification-constrained optimal transport and derives closed-form tradeoffs validated by deep compression models.
AI.motivation: Cross-domain lossy compression, where the encoder sees a degraded source and the decoder reconstructs a different target distribution, lacks unified theoretical tradeoffs involving rate, distortion, perception, and classification.
AI.method: The authors formulate the problem as constrained optimal transport with rate and classification constraints, derive closed-form DRC, RDC, and DRPC expressions for Bernoulli and Gaussian sources, and build deep end-to-end models.
AI.result: Experiments on super-resolution (MNIST), denoising (SVHN, CIFAR-10, ImageNet, KODAK), and inpainting (SVHN) demonstrate consistency between theoretical tradeoffs and empirical performance.
AI.conclusion: Constrained optimal transport provides a rigorous theoretical and practical foundation for cross-domain lossy compression.

title: Asymmetric Synthetic Data Update for Domain Incremental Dataset Distillation

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Domain Incremental Dataset Distillation and proposes Asymmetric Synthetic Data Update to mitigate catastrophic forgetting across sequentially arriving domains.
AI.motivation: Conventional dataset distillation assumes the full dataset is available upfront, whereas sequential distillation of incremental domains overwrites old knowledge and causes catastrophic forgetting.
AI.method: The authors propose Asymmetric Synthetic Data Update, which uses a bi-level meta-learning optimization to estimate per-sample update rates that balance stability and plasticity.
AI.result: Experimental results show that the proposed strategy mitigates catastrophic forgetting and outperforms existing methods on continually incoming datasets.
AI.conclusion: Per-sample asymmetric update rates enable effective continual dataset distillation across incremental domains.

title: An Optimal Diffusion Approach to Quadratic Rate-Distortion Problems: New Solution and Approximation Methods

AI.tldr: This paper formulates quadratic rate-distortion problems as stochastic optimal control via entropic optimal transport and derives exact solutions and diffusion-based numerical approximations.
AI.motivation: Computing the rate-distortion function for general continuous sources is challenging, motivating new analytical and numerical formulations.
AI.method: Exploiting connections to entropic optimal transport and Schrodinger's problem, the authors equate rate-MSE tradeoffs to control energy versus terminal differential entropy, solving backward heat equations for special sources and using constant-diffusion processes generally.
AI.result: Several numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the diffusion-based method in estimating the rate-distortion function.
AI.conclusion: Stochastic control and diffusion processes offer a principled framework for solving and approximating quadratic rate-distortion problems.

title: Interference-Isolated Elastic Weight Consolidation and Knowledge Calibration for Incremental Object Detection

AI.tldr: This paper proposes IKI-EWC and Prototype-based Knowledge Calibration (PKC) to isolate task conflicts and mitigate catastrophic forgetting in Incremental Object Detection.
AI.motivation: Existing incremental object detection methods lack quantitative modeling of information conflicts when unlabeled past and future objects appear as background in current-task images.
AI.method: IKI-EWC uses old detector mispredictions on new data to estimate and suppress parameter-level task conflicts, while PKC uses a learnable projection layer to compensate prototype semantic drift when training the classification head.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC and MS-COCO benchmarks show the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches across various incremental settings.
AI.conclusion: Isolating parameter-level task interference and calibrating old class prototypes significantly improves knowledge retention in incremental object detection.

title: Semi-Parametric Contextual Pricing with General Smoothness

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a unified contextual pricing algorithm for general beta-Holder link functions that achieves an optimal regret rate of O-tilde(T^((beta+1)/(2*beta+1))) for all beta >= 1.
AI.motivation: Prior semi-parametric contextual pricing analyses only covered specific smoothness values (beta=1 and beta=2, with a gap at beta=2) and relied on restrictive derivative lower bound assumptions.
AI.method: Under uni-modality, the authors combine a stationary subroutine with local polynomial regression and develop tighter semi-parametric confidence regions without derivative lower bound assumptions.
AI.result: The algorithm achieves regret O-tilde(T^((beta+1)/(2*beta+1))) for all beta >= 1, recovering and strengthening prior rates while reducing forced-exploration phases.
AI.conclusion: Tighter confidence regions and local polynomial regression unify and improve theoretical guarantees for smooth semi-parametric contextual pricing.

title: MMReD: a Cross-Modal Benchmark for Dense Context Reasoning

AI.tldr: MMReD is a 24-task cross-modal benchmark for dense context reasoning that reveals severe performance degradation in LLMs and LVLMs as context length increases.
AI.motivation: Standard Needle-in-a-Haystack evaluations only test simple retrieval, leaving models' ability to perform global reasoning over dense, information-rich multi-modal contexts underexplored.
AI.method: The authors construct MMReD with 24 tasks requiring selective or uniform attention across all context chunks and evaluate leading LLMs, LVLMs, and fine-tuned models up to 128 observations.
AI.result: All tested models drop sharply in performance as observations increase, with leading reasoning models hitting 0% accuracy on certain tasks at 128 observations, and SFT/GRPO failing to generalize to longer contexts.
AI.conclusion: Current model architectures and standard fine-tuning methods have fundamental limitations in dense multi-modal context reasoning.

title: Who Matters Matters: Agent-Specific Conservative Offline MARL

AI.tldr: OMCDA is an offline MARL framework that dynamically adjusts conservatism per agent based on behavior policy divergence and estimated agent importance.
AI.motivation: Existing offline MARL methods apply uniform conservatism across heterogeneous agents, over-constraining critical agents and under-constraining others, which harms team collaboration.
AI.method: OMCDA introduces a decomposed Q-function to separate return computation from policy deviation assessment and an adaptive conservatism mechanism scaled by divergence and agent importance.
AI.result: Experiments on MuJoCo and SMAC show OMCDA outperforms existing offline MARL methods, improving credit assignment and collaboration.
AI.conclusion: Agent-specific adaptive conservatism enables better flexibility-conservatism trade-offs in heterogeneous offline MARL.

title: How Transformers Learn Causal Structures In-Context: Explainable Mechanism Meets Theoretical Guarantee

AI.tldr: This paper proves and empirically shows that Transformers can learn causal structures in-context by approximating Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA).
AI.motivation: Theoretical analyses of in-context learning typically assume fixed dependency structures, whereas real-world sequences have context-dependent causal relationships.
AI.method: Using Markov chains with randomly sampled causal dependencies, the authors prove a two-layer Transformer with relative positional embeddings can implement BMA, analyze attention patterns, and derive information-theoretic recovery guarantees.
AI.result: Experiments and parameter-level analyses confirm that trained Transformers approximate BMA with attention reflecting inferred causal structures, and the analysis extends to continuous dynamical systems.
AI.conclusion: Transformers can perform sophisticated statistical inference over structural uncertainty in-context via BMA approximation.

title: Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models through Residual Learning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a two-stage LLM knowledge distillation framework using residual learning so students can improve beyond imperfect teacher representations.
AI.motivation: Intermediate-state distillation can mislead students when teacher knowledge is imperfect, and cross-tokenizer distillation requires handling vocabulary mismatches.
AI.method: Stage 1 pretrains projectors to compress teacher states via self-reconstruction; Stage 2 uses a hybrid objective with residual learning on the differential between student and projected teacher states, plus self-attention for MoE teachers and cross-model attention for cross-tokenizer settings.
AI.result: Experiments show superior performance under both same-tokenizer and cross-tokenizer settings, improving student generalization while preserving teacher knowledge.
AI.conclusion: Residual learning and attention-based alignment enable effective LLM distillation across architectures and tokenizers.

title: Hierarchical Value-Decomposed Offline Reinforcement Learning for Whole-Body Control

AI.tldr: HVD (Hierarchical Value-Decomposed Offline RL) learns high-DoF whole-body robot control from imperfect data by combining offline RL data selection with kinematic hierarchical value decomposition.
AI.motivation: Imitation learning for whole-body robots is limited by scarce expert demonstrations, while abundant suboptimal data is hard to exploit due to imperfect trajectories and high-dimensional control complexity.
AI.method: HVD uses a Transformer-based architecture with offline RL to prioritize high-value behaviors and hierarchical value decomposition along the robot's kinematic structure, trained on a new 50-hour imperfect dataset (WB-50).
AI.result: Experiments show HVD significantly outperforms existing baselines in success rate across complex whole-body tasks.
AI.conclusion: Structured offline RL over realistic, imperfect data can effectively scale whole-body robot control without relying on perfect demonstrations.

title: Plug-and-Play Compositionality for Boosting Continual Learning with Foundation Models

AI.tldr: CompSLOT is a plug-and-play concept-level framework that extracts semantic slots from pretrained vision transformers to mitigate catastrophic forgetting in continual learning.
AI.motivation: Continual vision learners rely on holistic class comparison rather than compositional concept understanding, leading to catastrophic forgetting especially when tasks have few classes.
AI.method: CompSLOT extracts semantically meaningful slots from ImageNet-pretrained ViTs, applies primitive selection and aggregation, and uses method-agnostic self-supervision to distill concept-based similarity into the classifier.
AI.result: Experiments show CompSLOT significantly enhances diverse continual learning baselines as a universal concept-level module.
AI.conclusion: Injecting plug-and-play concept compositionality into foundation-model continual learners effectively reduces catastrophic forgetting.

title: Towards Persistent Noise-Tolerant Active Learning of Regular Languages with Class Query

AI.tldr: CAPAL is an active learning algorithm for deterministic finite automata (DFAs) that remains correct under persistent membership query noise using statistical class queries and a discrimination tree.
AI.motivation: LLMs acting as fallible oracles in formal synthesis produce noisy, inconsistent membership answers, breaking classic active automata learning algorithms like L*.
AI.method: CAPAL augments L* with a statistical same-state class query comparing prefix disagreements against a micro-bootstrapped noise-floor estimate with Hoeffding tolerances, and a discrimination tree for near-minimal discriminators.
AI.result: The authors prove convergence given a perfect equivalence oracle and show substantial membership-query savings and robustness on benchmarks including RegexLib and KB13.
AI.conclusion: Noise-tolerant active DFA learning enables reliable synthesis of verifiable formal artifacts from fallible LLM collaborators.

title: Bayesian Test-Time Adaptation via Dirichlet feature projection and GMM-Driven Inference for Motor Imagery EEG Decoding

AI.tldr: BTTA-DG is a gradient-free Bayesian test-time adaptation framework for motor imagery EEG decoding using Dirichlet feature projection and GMM-driven inference.
AI.motivation: Cross-subject and cross-session variability hinders EEG-BCI generalization, while existing test-time adaptation methods either require costly gradient updates or fail to model temporal predictive embedding shifts.
AI.method: BTTA-DG extracts frequency bands via SincAdaptNet, maps temporal embeddings to a Dirichlet parameter space, and calibrates target predictions using GMM-driven Bayesian inference over historical Dirichlet parameters.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show BTTA-DG achieves state-of-the-art accuracy at real-time speed, with visualizations confirming physiological filter interpretability and class separability.
AI.conclusion: Gradient-free Bayesian adaptation in Dirichlet space provides fast, interpretable, and accurate test-time adaptation for EEG decoding.

title: GOOD: Geometry-guided Out-of-Distribution Modeling for Open-set Test-time Adaptation in Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation

AI.tldr: GOOD is a geometry-guided out-of-distribution modeling strategy for open-set test-time adaptation (OSTTA) in 3D point cloud semantic segmentation.
AI.motivation: Applying OSTTA to 3D point clouds is hindered by severe imbalance between dominant in-distribution (ID) points and sparse or absent out-of-distribution (OOD) instances.
AI.method: GOOD clusters point clouds into superpoints using geometric priors, introduces a confidence metric to separate ID and OOD superpoints, and uses prototype-based representations to sharpen ID/OOD discrimination.
AI.result: Validated across four benchmarks, GOOD outperforms HGL on Synth4D to SemanticKITTI by 1.93% mIoU, 8.99% AUROC, and 7.91% FPR95.
AI.conclusion: Superpoint geometric priors and prototype representations effectively address ID/OOD imbalance in 3D open-set test-time adaptation.

title: PRO-MOF: Policy Optimization with Universal Atomistic Models for Controllable MOF Generation

AI.tldr: PRO-MOF is a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework with universal atomistic model rewards and Pass@K GRPO for controllable metal-organic framework (MOF) generation.
AI.motivation: Existing generative models for inverse MOF design struggle to explore vast chemical and structural spaces, often suffering from suboptimal solutions or mode collapse.
AI.method: PRO-MOF decouples design into a high-level building-block policy and a low-level 3D assembly policy (converting Flow Matching into an SDE), optimized in a closed loop with a universal atomistic model and Pass@K GRPO.
AI.result: On inverse design tasks such as maximizing CO2 working capacity and targeting pore diameters, PRO-MOF outperforms diffusion baselines and genetic algorithms in success rate and top-performing material discovery.
AI.conclusion: Combining hierarchical RL, SDE-based exploration, and physical atomistic rewards advances controllable material discovery.

title: PAMDP: Interact to Persona Alignment via a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process

AI.tldr: This paper formulates interactive persona alignment as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (PAMDP) and solves it with a dual-critic reinforcement learning framework.
AI.motivation: Aligning Persona LLMs to dynamically evolving user-specific preferences during dialogue requires modeling genuine interaction dynamics rather than static general human values.
AI.method: PAMDP treats the user's evolving profile as an unobservable state and uses a dual-critic RL framework with continuous latent-space actions representing assistant utterances.
AI.result: Evaluations on both offline datasets and an online simulator demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
AI.conclusion: Modeling user profiles as latent states in a POMDP provides a principled framework for interactive persona alignment.

title: Minimax Optimal Adversarial Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: This paper proves that sublinear regret is achievable in episodic MDPs with fully adversarial transition kernels and presents the minimax optimal AD-FTRL algorithm.
AI.motivation: Prior work on adversarial MDPs achieved regret bounds with a linear-scaling change term C^P, leaving open whether sublinear regret is possible under fully adversarial transitions.
AI.method: The authors show optimal policies must be history-dependent and design Adversarial Dynamics Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (AD-FTRL).
AI.result: AD-FTRL achieves sublinear regret O(sqrt((|S||A|)^K * T)), and a matching lower bound proves its minimax optimality.
AI.conclusion: History-dependent FTRL resolves the open question of sublinear regret in fully adversarial transition MDPs with minimax optimality.

title: CortiLife: A Unified Framework for Cortical Representation Learning across the Lifespan

AI.tldr: CortiLife is a unified vision-language framework for lifespan-aware cortical representation learning using a multi-level surface tokenizer and metadata language prompting.
AI.motivation: Existing cortical representation models are limited to stage-specific cohorts and struggle with non-Euclidean manifolds, registration-induced homogenization, and lifespan distribution shifts.
AI.method: CortiLife uses an icosahedron-based surface tokenizer with three complementary encoding streams (local topology, global interactions, patch distributions) alongside masked self-distillation and metadata language prompting.
AI.result: Across two encoder-frozen tasks (age prediction, cortical parcellation) and four fine-tuning tasks (brain disorder diagnosis), CortiLife consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across age stages and modalities.
AI.conclusion: Multi-level surface tokenization and metadata prompting enable generalizable cortical representation learning across the human lifespan.

title: VoG: Enhancing LLM Reasoning through Stepwise Verification on Knowledge Graphs

AI.tldr: Verify-on-Graph (VoG) is a model-agnostic framework that improves LLM reasoning via iterative knowledge graph retrieval, stepwise verification, and bandit-guided plan revision.
AI.motivation: Existing KG-augmented LLM frameworks use static integration mechanisms that cannot adapt reasoning to evolving context and evidence, causing error propagation.
AI.method: VoG iteratively retrieves KG evidence, verifies reasoning steps, and revises the reasoning plan using a context-aware multi-armed bandit guided by uncertainty and semantic consistency rewards.
AI.result: Experiments across three benchmark datasets show VoG consistently improves both reasoning accuracy and efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive, stepwise verification and revision on knowledge graphs significantly reduce hallucinations and improve LLM reasoning.

title: Low-Rank Few-Shot Node Classification by Node-Level Graph Diffusion

AI.tldr: LR-FGDM combines a node-level graph diffusion model with low-rank transductive classification and an efficient LR-Attention layer for few-shot node classification.
AI.motivation: Few-shot node classification suffers from scarce labeled support sets, while diffusion-based graph augmentation introduces noise that degrades transductive classification.
AI.method: LR-FGDM generates an augmented graph via a Hierarchical Graph Autoencoder and Latent Diffusion Model, then applies low-rank transductive classification (with theoretical guarantees) and an LR-Attention layer to reduce kernel complexity.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show LR-FGDM and LRA-LR-FGDM outperform current state-of-the-art methods on few-shot node classification.
AI.conclusion: Low-rank regularization and efficient attention effectively mitigate diffusion noise and improve generalization in few-shot node classification.

title: HippoTune: A Hippocampal Associative Loop–Inspired Fine-Tuning Method for Continual Learning

AI.tldr: HippoTune is a continual learning fine-tuning method inspired by hippocampal associative recall that embeds an iterative query-retrieve-feedback loop inside each Transformer layer.
AI.motivation: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) freezes most weights to reduce forgetting but struggles to reactivate old task memories without replay buffers.
AI.method: HippoTune performs iterative soft key-value retrieval from hidden states within each Transformer layer, which theoretically implements a Krylov-style polynomial approximation equivalent to a differentiable second-order preconditioner.
AI.result: Across three vision benchmarks, HippoTune outperforms classical buffer-free PEFT-CL methods by 5-8% in accuracy while reducing training FLOPs by 50%.
AI.conclusion: Hippocampal-inspired iterative latent retrieval effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting under tight compute budgets without replay buffers.

title: On the Universality and Complexity of GNN for Solving Second-order Cone Programs

AI.tldr: This paper establishes universal approximation and Rademacher generalization bounds for Graph Neural Networks solving Second-Order Cone Programs (SOCPs) and general p-order cone programs.
AI.motivation: While GNNs have been theoretically justified for linear and quadratic programming, universality and generalization guarantees for more general convex conic programs like SOCPs remained unexplored.
AI.method: The authors propose a graph representation capturing conic constraints, prove a universality theorem for feasibility and optimal solutions, and derive Rademacher complexity sample bounds extending to any p >= 1.
AI.result: Numerical experiments on random SOCPs and real-world power grid problems show superior prediction accuracy with significantly fewer parameters than fully connected networks.
AI.conclusion: GNNs provide a theoretically grounded, parameter-efficient paradigm for data-driven conic optimization solvers.

title: M$^3$E: Continual Vision-and-Language Navigation via Mixture of Macro and Micro Experts

AI.tldr: M^3E is an environment-aware hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts framework for continual Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) that decouples global scene reasoning from local perceptual alignment.
AI.motivation: VLN agents suffer from catastrophic forgetting when continually adapting to new environments without revisiting prior data.
AI.method: M^3E uses a macro-level scene-aware router for strategy experts, a micro-level instance-aware router for perception experts, and a dynamic momentum update strategy to selectively update or freeze experts.
AI.result: Evaluated in domain-incremental settings on R2R and REVERIE, M^3E consistently outperforms standard fine-tuning and continual learning baselines in adaptability and retention.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling macro and micro experts with selective momentum updates enables parameter-efficient continual learning for embodied navigation.

title: Information-Theoretic Membership Inference for Granular Quantification of Memorization

AI.tldr: InfoRMIA is an information-theoretic membership inference attack that outperforms RMIA and enables token-level localization of memorization in LLMs.
AI.motivation: Sequence-level membership inference obscures which specific tokens in LLM outputs are memorized, limiting fine-grained privacy assessment.
AI.method: The authors formulate InfoRMIA from information-theoretic principles and build a token-level memorization assessment framework using InfoRMIA as its backbone.
AI.result: InfoRMIA consistently outperforms RMIA across benchmarks with higher computational efficiency and successfully localizes privacy leakage to individual memorized tokens.
AI.conclusion: Information-theoretic token-level membership inference enables precise memorization auditing and targeted mitigation such as exact unlearning.

title: Scaling Goal-conditioned Reinforcement Learning with Multistep Quasimetric Distances

AI.tldr: This paper integrates multistep Monte-Carlo returns into quasimetric distance learning to scale goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL) to long-horizon visual and real-world robotic tasks.
AI.motivation: Quasimetric GCRL methods struggle in stochastic, high-dimensional visual environments due to the tension between local TD backups and global Monte-Carlo returns.
AI.method: The authors fit a quasimetric distance representation using multistep Monte-Carlo returns, balancing shortest-path inductive bias with stable statistical estimation.
AI.result: The method outperforms existing GCRL baselines on simulated tasks up to 4000 steps with visual observations and enables end-to-end multistep stitching on real-world Bridge robotic manipulation from unlabeled offline data.
AI.conclusion: Combining quasimetric inductive biases with multistep returns unlocks scalable long-horizon visual GCRL in real-world robotics.

title: MoL: Adaptive Mixture-of-Length Reasoning for Efficient Question Answering with Context

AI.tldr: Mixture-of-Length (MoL) is an adaptive reasoning approach for contextual QA that modulates response length based on query difficulty.
AI.motivation: Standard QA models do not adaptively balance reasoning quality and token efficiency across queries of varying complexity.
AI.method: MoL uses information-theoretic difficulty assessment and a dual-objective reward mechanism to dynamically adjust response length.
AI.result: Across multiple QA benchmarks, MoL achieves competitive accuracy while substantially reducing token usage, exhibiting "intelligent brevity" correlated with the effective number of contributing layers.
AI.conclusion: Difficulty-aware length modulation offers a promising path toward efficient, adaptive contextual question answering.

title: Retain and Adapt: Auto-Balanced Model Editing for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection under Domain Shifts

AI.tldr: Automatically Balanced Model Editing (ABME) enables order-agnostic continual adaptation of Open-Vocabulary Object Detection (OVOD) models under domain shifts without retraining.
AI.motivation: OVOD performance drops under OOD shifts, while existing continual learning methods struggle to balance retention and adaptation and depend on task ordering.
AI.method: ABME stores compact key-value matrices with task-volume-independent storage cost and uses them to automatically balance old and new knowledge, supporting order-agnostic task insertion or removal.
AI.result: Experiments show ABME achieves a better retention-adaptation trade-off than existing continual learning methods for OVOD across different models and task scales.
AI.conclusion: Model editing with balanced key-value storage provides an efficient, order-agnostic solution for continual OVOD under domain shifts.

title: Leveraging Explanation to Improve Generalization of Meta Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a two-stage bilevel optimization approach using conditional mutual information to identify and augment critical training tasks, improving meta-reinforcement learning generalization.
AI.motivation: Meta-reinforcement learning (MRL) often suffers from imbalanced generalization, adapting well to some tasks while performing poorly on others.
AI.method: The first stage identifies critical training tasks relevant to poorly adapted tasks; the second stage formulates a bilevel optimization problem maximizing conditional mutual information via task augmentation.
AI.result: The authors prove O(1/sqrt(K)) convergence and improved generalization, validating the algorithm on two real-world experiments, two MuJoCo tasks, and Meta-World.
AI.conclusion: Explanation-driven identification and augmentation of critical tasks provably and empirically improves MRL generalization.

title: Group Verification-based Policy Optimization for Interactive Coding Agents

AI.tldr: Group Verification-based Policy Optimization (GVPO) integrates outcome-verifiable rewards and step-level process-verifiable execution feedback to improve interactive coding agents.
AI.motivation: Existing RLVR methods like GRPO ignore intermediate process-verifiable environment feedback (e.g., execution errors), causing inaccurate step-level advantage estimation.
AI.method: GVPO introduces an advantage shaping framework that combines long-term outcome rewards with corrective step-level shaping terms derived from intermediate execution traces.
AI.result: A 32B-parameter agent trained with GVPO on AppWorld outperforms OpenAI's o1 agent by 12.7% on Test-C and surpasses the strongest 32B RL baseline by 3.7%.
AI.conclusion: Jointly leveraging outcome and process verifiability yields more accurate credit assignment and stronger generalization for interactive coding agents.

title: Negotiated Reasoning: On Provably Addressing Relative Over-Generalization

AI.tldr: Stein Variational Negotiated Reasoning (SVNR) is a theoretically grounded MARL algorithm that provably avoids relative over-generalization (RO) in fully cooperative tasks.
AI.motivation: While reasoning helps mitigate relative over-generalization in cooperative MARL empirically, theoretical guarantees connecting reasoning and RO avoidance were lacking.
AI.method: The authors prove a consistent reasoning requirement avoids RO, formulate a negotiated reasoning framework, and use Stein variational gradient descent with neural parameterization to form a negotiation policy under maximum-entropy policy iteration.
AI.result: Experiments on RO-challenged tasks including Multi-Agent Particle World and MaMuJoCo show SVNR significantly outperforms baselines in achieving cooperation.
AI.conclusion: Negotiated reasoning via Stein variational gradient descent provides provable and practical mitigation of relative over-generalization.

title: An Information-Theoretic Parameter-Free Bayesian Framework for Probing Labeled Dependency Trees from Attention Score

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an information-theoretic, parameter-free Bayesian framework to estimate mutual information and extract labeled dependency trees directly from LLM attention scores.
AI.motivation: Existing syntactic probing methods require training additional auxiliary networks and struggle with complex dependency trees and fine-grained interpretability.
AI.method: The framework mathematically estimates mutual information and extracts dependency trees directly from attention scores without any extra network training.
AI.result: Evaluations across several open-source LLMs show the method outperforms competitive probing baselines while remaining simpler and more transparent.
AI.conclusion: Parameter-free information-theoretic probing offers a clean, interpretable way to uncover syntactic comprehension in LLMs.

title: On Coreset for LASSO Regression Problem with Sensitivity Sampling

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an empirical process-based sensitivity sampling method for LASSO regression that achieves a tighter coreset size bound and a 4x to 9x+ empirical speedup over existing solvers.
AI.motivation: Extending sensitivity sampling from unregularized regression to LASSO typically yields coreset sizes scaling with O(G d) because it is difficult to capture the sparse, localized structure of the function space induced by the l1 penalty.
AI.method: The authors localize sensitivity sampling for LASSO by decomposing the functional space into separate components and leveraging their geometric properties to derive tight empirical process bounds on coreset size.
AI.result: The method achieves a (1 +/- epsilon)-approximation coreset of size tilde-O(epsilon^-2 d (log^3 d * min{1, log d / lambda^2} + log(1/delta))) and a matching Omega(d log d / epsilon^2) lower bound for lambda = O(d^-1/2); empirically it is at least 4x faster than existing LASSO solvers and over 9x faster on half the datasets while preserving solution quality and sparsity.
AI.conclusion: Localized empirical process sensitivity sampling provides both near-optimal theoretical coreset bounds and substantial practical speedups for LASSO regression.

title: Robust Selective Activation with Randomized Temporal K-Winner-Take-All in Spiking Neural Networks for Continual Learning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Randomized Temporal K-winner-take-all (RTK-WTA) for spiking neural networks, improving continual learning accuracy by 3.07 to 5.0% over deterministic K-WTA.
AI.motivation: Continual learning in spiking neural networks (SNNs) struggles to balance task-specific selectivity, adaptive resource allocation, and robustness to temporal perturbations to mitigate catastrophic forgetting.
AI.method: RTK-WTA integrates trace-dependent neuronal activation with probabilistic top-k selection, dynamically prioritizing neurons by spatiotemporal relevance while introducing controlled randomness to prevent overlapping task representations.
AI.result: Theoretically, RTK-WTA enhances inter-class margins and robustness via expanded feature space utilization; experimentally, it surpasses deterministic K-WTA by 3.07 to 5.0% accuracy on splitMNIST and splitCIFAR100 with elastic weight consolidation.
AI.conclusion: Controlled stochasticity in temporal winner-take-all competition balances temporal coherence and adaptability for scalable lifelong learning in neuromorphic systems.

title: Detect, Decide, Unlearn: A Transfer-Aware Framework for Continual Learning

AI.tldr: This paper introduces DEDUCE, a continual learning framework that detects negative transfer and applies hybrid local and global unlearning, improving average accuracy by up to 4.55% over baselines.
AI.motivation: Most continual learning (CL) methods focus on preventing catastrophic forgetting, but retaining outdated knowledge can cause negative transfer that interferes with new task learning and impairs adaptability.
AI.method: DEDUCE detects negative transfer using transferability bounds and gradient conflict analysis, then decides whether to activate a Local Unlearning Module (LUM) to filter outdated knowledge before learning a new task, alongside a Global Unlearning Module (GUM) that periodically reclaims model capacity.
AI.result: Experiments show that DEDUCE mitigates task interference and improves overall accuracy with an average gain of up to 4.55% over state-of-the-art baselines.
AI.conclusion: Selectively unlearning interfering prior knowledge complements memory preservation and enhances plasticity in continual learning.

title: Learning to Reason over Continuous Tokens with Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes HyRea, a framework that trains LLMs via supervised cold-start and GRPO reinforcement learning to dynamically switch between explicit token-based and latent embedding-based reasoning.
AI.motivation: Discrete Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning incurs high computational and memory costs due to verbose steps, whereas prior latent reasoning in embedding space often sacrifices clarity and performance.
AI.method: HyRea uses a two-stage pipeline: a supervised cold-start phase that replaces low-entropy CoT steps with embeddings, followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) reinforcement learning to fine-tune the switching strategy using task-specific rewards.
AI.result: Experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks show that HyRea significantly reduces token usage while maintaining or improving accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Dynamically combining explicit and latent reasoning offers an effective, scalable path to efficient multi-step reasoning in LLMs.

title: Minimax Sample Complexity of Graph Neural Networks: Lower Bounds and Structural Effects

AI.tldr: This paper establishes minimax sample complexity bounds for ReLU message-passing GNNs, showing that practical graph benchmarks operate in a spectral-homophily regime with d / log n scaling rather than 1 / sqrt(n).
AI.motivation: Despite strong empirical performance, the fundamental statistical behavior and sample complexity of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) under explicit architectural and structural assumptions remain poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors derive minimax generalization bounds for ReLU message-passing GNNs in both inductive and transductive settings, analyzing arbitrary graphs versus graphs satisfying a spectral-homophily condition (strong label homophily and bounded spectral expansion).
AI.result: For arbitrary graphs, worst-case error scales as sqrt(log d / n), whereas under spectral-homophily transductive node prediction has a minimax lower bound of d / log n; empirical scaling tests on ogbn_arxiv, ogbn_products_50k, Reddit_50k, and synthetic datasets confirm that real benchmarks follow the d / log n rate while worst-case synthetic graphs follow sqrt(log d / n).
AI.conclusion: Effective sample complexity in practical GNN tasks is governed by graph topology in the spectral-homophily regime rather than universal 1 / sqrt(n) behavior.

title: Divide and Abstract: Autoformalization via Decomposition and Abstraction Learning

AI.tldr: This paper presents Divide and Abstract (DNA), a zero-training autoformalization framework that learns reusable corpus-level abstractions and hierarchically decomposes statements, achieving up to 8.6x gains on benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM-based autoformalization methods rely on pre-defined libraries and direct full-statement generation, which bottlenecks them on existing abstractions, complex statements, and cross-language transfer.
AI.method: DNA operates in two training-free phases: first extracting common mathematical concepts across a corpus as reusable formal abstractions, and second hierarchically decomposing new statements into informal clauses, translating each with the learned abstractions, and composing them.
AI.result: On LeanEuclidPlus and ProofNet-Hard, DNA achieves up to 8.6x performance gains over baselines across multiple model families, enables smaller models to match much larger baselines, and excels on nested reasoning without target-language training.
AI.conclusion: Corpus-level abstraction learning paired with hierarchical decomposition provides an effective, training-free paradigm for autoformalization, including in low-resource formal languages.

title: Variational Inference for Cyclic Learning

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates cyclic learning as variational inference over conditional probability mappings, yielding general single-step and alternating optimization strategies applied to unpaired image translation and unsupervised tracking.
AI.motivation: Cyclic learning with inverse task pairs and cycle-consistency losses is widely used in weakly-supervised learning, but existing methods are narrowly tied to domain-specific implementations without a unified theoretical foundation.
AI.method: The authors model cross-domain mappings as conditional probability functions, reformulate cycle-consistency as evidence lower bound (ELBO) optimization via variational inference, and derive single-step and alternating optimization strategies for pairwise and self-cycle-consistent tasks.
AI.result: The framework provides theoretical justification for CycleGAN, yields a competitive GAN-free alternative called CycleGN for unpaired image translation, and produces CycleTrack and CycleTrack-EM, which achieve state-of-the-art results on multiple unsupervised tracking benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Variational inference establishes a unified theoretical foundation and general optimization paradigm for cyclic learning across diverse weakly-supervised tasks.

title: Balancing the Experts: Unlocking LoRA-MoE for GRPO via Mechanism-Aware Rewards

AI.tldr: This paper introduces RO-GRPO, a mechanism-aware reinforcement fine-tuning framework that converts internal LoRA-MoE routing statistics into a reward signal to prevent routing collapse.
AI.motivation: Fine-tuning LoRA-MoE architectures with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) suffers from routing collapse and underutilized adapter parameters because traditional supervised balancing techniques are incompatible with GRPO.
AI.method: Routing-Optimized GRPO (RO-GRPO) collects internal expert routing statistics during training and turns them into a scalar reward signal integrated directly into the GRPO objective without extra training stages.
AI.result: RO-GRPO improves parameter utilization and boosts performance on both unimodal and multimodal mathematical reasoning tasks.
AI.conclusion: Engineering rewards from a model's own internal routing mechanics extends GRPO alignment from behavior tuning to holistic mechanism alignment.

title: Instance-Dependent Fixed-Budget Pure Exploration in Reinforcement Learning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes fixed-budget pure exploration algorithms for reinforcement learning with the first instance-dependent epsilon-uniform guarantees, without requiring target error or failure rate inputs.
AI.motivation: Standard PAC pure exploration in reinforcement learning requires specifying target error epsilon and failure rate delta in advance, leaving fixed-budget pure exploration without instance-dependent guarantees across error levels.
AI.method: The authors develop novel fixed-budget RL algorithms, alongside an epsilon-uniform guarantee for solving multiple multi-armed bandit instances simultaneously and new tools for fixed-budget reward-free exploration.
AI.result: They establish the first instance-dependent epsilon-uniform guarantee in fixed-budget RL, ensuring epsilon-correctness simultaneously for all epsilon above a budget-dependent threshold characterized by problem-specific exploration hardness.
AI.conclusion: The proposed algorithms and reward-free exploration tools provide instance-dependent fixed-budget guarantees that eliminate the need for pre-specified accuracy and confidence parameters.

title: Escaping Policy Contraction: Contraction-Aware PPO (CaPPO) for Stable Language Model Fine-Tuning

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Contraction-Aware PPO (CaPPO) to mitigate policy support contraction in RLHF, improving win rates by 2 to 4 points and diversity (SRR) by 0.2 to 0.3 over standard PPO.
AI.motivation: On-policy RLHF with PPO often reduces output diversity compared to supervised fine-tuning (SFT), a phenomenon the authors formalize as policy contraction via the Support Retention Ratio (SRR).
AI.method: CaPPO uses a minimum-norm multi-gradient update to co-optimize reward, token entropy, and KL divergence to the reference policy, paired with a controller that steers exploration toward a target token entropy.
AI.result: Across HH-RLHF, Summarize-from-Feedback, and UltraFeedback using Qwen2-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Llama-3-8B-Instruct, CaPPO increases win rate by 2 to 4 points and gains 0.2 to 0.3 higher SRR over PPO, remaining robust across decoding sweeps, reward scaling, and critic variance.
AI.conclusion: Treating reward, diversity, and stability as first-class objectives enables CaPPO to prevent policy contraction without sacrificing alignment performance.

title: PepTri: Tri-Guided All-Atom Diffusion for Peptide Design via Physics, Evolution, and Mutual Information

AI.tldr: This paper introduces PepTri, an SE(3)-equivariant all-atom diffusion model that jointly generates peptide sequences and 3D structures using physics, evolutionary, and mutual information guidance.
AI.motivation: Existing deep generative models for peptide design are often structure-centric and decouple sequence and structure generation, failing to ensure physical stability, evolutionary plausibility, and internal coherence simultaneously.
AI.method: PepTri jointly generates peptide sequences and 3D structures in a unified SE(3)-equivariant latent space, steering denoising with differentiable molecular mechanics physics guidance, evolutionary motif guidance, and mutual information guidance for sequence-structure coherence.
AI.result: Evaluations on cross-domain (PepBench, LNR) and in-domain (PepBDB) peptide-protein design benchmarks show that PepTri substantially outperforms strong baselines, achieving state-of-the-art binding affinity, structural accuracy, and design diversity.
AI.conclusion: Integrating biophysical, evolutionary, and information-theoretic guidance directly into all-atom denoising is crucial for generating viable peptide therapeutics.

title: OR-PRM: A Process Reward Model for Algorithmic Problem in Operations Research

AI.tldr: This paper introduces OR-ProcessQA and OR-PRM, the first step-level dataset and Process Reward Model for Operations Research, improving LLM Best-of-N reasoning by up to 12.5% over the base model.
AI.motivation: Applying Process Reward Models (PRMs) to Operations Research (OR) has been unexplored, and training directly on existing synthetic OR datasets fails because over 30% of their annotations are severely flawed.
AI.method: The authors filter existing synthetic datasets into a clean seed, construct OR-ProcessQA by generating diverse solution paths with MCTS and validating each step via GPT-4o, and train OR-PRM to score and guide intermediate reasoning steps.
AI.result: OR-PRM substantially improves LLM reasoning in Operations Research, achieving up to a 12.5% absolute improvement over the base model in Best-of-N settings.
AI.conclusion: High-quality step-by-step process supervision unlocks reliable LLM problem solving in Operations Research.

title: Random Anchors with Low-rank Decorrelated Learning: A Minimalist Pipeline for Class-Incremental Medical Image Classification

AI.tldr: This paper proposes RA-LDL, a minimalist representation-calibration pipeline for class-incremental medical image classification that outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods across four medical datasets.
AI.motivation: Complex pre-trained model (PTM) class-incremental learning (CIL) methods such as prompt tuning and task-specific adapters often suffer from representation collapse and domain misalignment in medical imaging due to low intra-class variability and high inter-domain shifts.
AI.method: Random Anchors with Low-rank Decorrelated Learning (RA-LDL) combines PTM feature extraction (with optional ViT-Adapter tuning), feature calibration via frozen Random Anchor projection and a single-session Low-Rank Projection (LRP), and analytical closed-form decorrelated learning.
AI.result: Requiring only one training session, RA-LDL achieves consistent gains across general-domain and medical-specific PTMs and outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods on four diverse medical imaging datasets.
AI.conclusion: Minimalist representation recalibration offers a practical, efficient, and extensible alternative to complex architectural modifications for medical CIL.

title: Meta-UCF: Unified Task-Conditioned LoRA Generation for Continual Learning in Large Language Models

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Meta-UCF, a continual learning method for LLMs that uses a hypernetwork and orthogonalized task embeddings to generate LoRA updates on the fly, cutting forgetting by 13% with constant memory.
AI.motivation: Existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods for continual learning in LLMs either grow linearly in memory with the number of tasks or fail to prevent catastrophic forgetting.
AI.method: Meta-Unified Contrastive Finetuning (Meta-UCF) encodes each task into a layer-normalized mean embedding, feeds it to a single hypernetwork to generate rank-r LoRA updates for every transformer layer, and applies a meta-contrastive orthogonality objective to keep task embeddings near-orthogonal without inner-loop gradients.
AI.result: On Std-CL 5, Seq-GLUE 7, Long-CL 15, and TRACE-8, Meta-UCF improves average accuracy by up to 2.2 percentage points and reduces forgetting by 13% over the strongest LoRA baseline while using the parameters of a single adapter.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling continual learning from parameter growth via task-conditioned LoRA generation enables scalable, memory-constant lifelong language modeling.

title: QuRL: Rubrics As Judge For Open-Ended Question Answering

AI.tldr: This paper introduces QuRL, a framework that mines question-specific rubrics from online sources and uses them as GRPO rewards for open-ended QA, achieving a +17.0 point improvement.
AI.motivation: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is hard to apply to open-ended QA because gold ground truth is absent, and existing human feedback or LLM-as-judge methods are costly, prone to reward hacking, and lack discriminative interpretability.
AI.method: QuRL defines a schema for question-specific, content-based, and stylistically sensitive case-wise rubrics, automatically mines them from online sources, and uses them as reward signals in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that QuRL achieves a +17.0 point total improvement on the evaluation benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Automated rubric-guided reinforcement learning provides an effective, interpretable alternative to LLM-as-judge for open-ended question answering.

title: Empowering LLM Tool Invocation with Tool-call Reward Model

AI.tldr: This paper proposes the Tool-call Reward Model (TRM), a process reward model for individual LLM tool invocations that outperforms outcome-only RL on search QA and Python math tasks.
AI.motivation: Outcome-only RL for LLM tool use assigns coarse credit and causes gradient conflicts, while adapting traditional process reward models to tool calls faces data/sizing unknowns and reward hacking in PPO/GRPO.
AI.method: The authors establish a systematic TRM construction workflow and introduce refined credit assignment and turn-level advantage estimation to integrate TRM with PPO and GRPO without reward hacking.
AI.result: Experiments show a 3B TRM trained on 10K samples performs robustly, and integrating TRM consistently outperforms outcome-only reward RL across model sizes on search-based QA and Python code-based math tasks.
AI.conclusion: Turn-level process rewards with tailored credit assignment enable more effective and reliable reinforcement learning for agentic tool invocation.

title: Following the Navigation: Enhancing Small Language Models Contextual Reasoning with LLM Guidance

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Navigation, a training-free framework that distills LLM contextual reasoning into reusable navigation templates for SLMs, yielding a 10.7% average accuracy gain.
AI.motivation: Small language models (SLMs) are efficient for resource-constrained deployment but struggle with contextual reasoning, while existing enhancement methods like distillation and data synthesis require additional training.
AI.method: Navigation distills LLM-derived contextual processing expertise into generalizable templates stored in a Navigation database, guiding SLMs through Generation, Utilization, and Update stages to locate and process key context information without training.
AI.result: Using a template count of at most 2.1% of the dataset size, Navigation achieves an average 10.7% accuracy gain and enables Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct to outperform GPT-3.5-Turbo on diverse contextual reasoning tasks.
AI.conclusion: Training-free navigation templates offer a lightweight, scalable way to bridge the contextual reasoning gap between SLMs and larger LLMs.

title: Learning Heterogeneous Degradation Representation for Real-World Super-Resolution

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Spatially Amortized Variational Learning (SAVL) to model per-pixel heterogeneous degradations for real-world super-resolution, achieving consistent gains over prior methods.
AI.motivation: Existing degradation representations for Real-World Super-Resolution (RWSR) struggle with spatially variant degradation modeling and entanglement between degradation and image content.
AI.method: SAVL models per-pixel degradations as spatially varying Gaussians inferred from local neighborhoods by coupling a conditional likelihood lane (SAVL-LM) with a mutual information suppression lane (SAVL-MIS), which then guides a degradation-aware SR network via channel-wise guidance and spatial attention modulation.
AI.result: Qualitative visualizations, quantitative analyses, and extensive experiments on real-world datasets confirm that SAVL captures discriminative, spatially varying degradations and consistently outperforms prior RWSR methods.
AI.conclusion: Disentangling and modeling spatially variant degradations via amortized variational learning improves adaptive reconstruction in real-world super-resolution.

title: Bandit Learning in Matching Markets Robust to Adversarial Corruptions

AI.tldr: This paper develops corruption-robust bandit algorithms for two-sided decentralized matching markets under both known and unknown adversarial corruption levels, with matching upper and lower regret bounds.
AI.motivation: In decentralized matching markets, stochastic reward feedback can be corrupted by malicious adversaries, misleading online preference learning and causing convergence to suboptimal matches.
AI.method: The authors propose a robust Explore-Then-Gale-Shapley (ETGS) variant with widened confidence intervals for known corruption level C, and a Multi-layer ETGS race method that adaptively mitigates corruptions when C is unknown.
AI.result: They establish theoretical upper bounds on optimal stable regret for both algorithms and derive a matching lower bound demonstrating their optimality.
AI.conclusion: Widened confidence intervals and multi-layer racing provide provably optimal robustness against adversarial corruptions in decentralized matching markets.

title: Language Identification in the Limit with Computational Trace

AI.tldr: This paper formalizes language identification in the limit with computational traces, proving that all computable languages become identifiable with perfect traces and establishing error-tolerance trichotomies under partial or corrupted traces.
AI.motivation: While Chain-of-Thought (CoT) training dramatically improves LLM capabilities empirically, a formal theoretical understanding of how computational traces affect learnability is lacking.
AI.method: The authors introduce identification in the limit with trace, augmenting Gold's 1967 paradigm by giving the learner both language examples and computational traces from the accepting machine, and analyze both perfect and partially corrupted trace settings.
AI.result: With perfect traces, all computable languages (Turing-machine recognizable) become identifiable in the limit, overcoming Gold's impossibility result even for deterministic finite automata; under partial and adversarially corrupted traces, the authors establish trichotomic error-tolerance results across the Chomsky hierarchy.
AI.conclusion: Computational traces fundamentally expand formal language learnability, offering theoretical grounding for the power of Chain-of-Thought supervision.

title: DiffPBR: Point-Based Rendering via Spatial-Aware Residual Diffusion

AI.tldr: This paper presents DiffPBR, a spatial-aware residual diffusion framework for point-based rendering that improves image quality by 3 to 5 dB while cutting training time and boosting rendering speed to 10 fps.
AI.motivation: Achieving high-fidelity, view-consistent novel view synthesis directly from point clouds without costly per-scene optimization remains a core challenge for neural rendering.
AI.method: DiffPBR combines adaptive CoNo-Splatting for fast point cloud rasterization with a residual diffusion neural re-rendering pipeline guided by viewpoint-projected noise constrained by scene geometry and visibility.
AI.result: Experiments show DiffPBR outperforms baselines by 3 to 5 dB in rendered image quality, reduces training from 41 to 8 GPU hours, and increases rendering speed from 3.6 fps to 10 fps with a one-step variant.
AI.conclusion: Geometry-constrained residual diffusion enables fast, view-consistent, high-fidelity point cloud rendering without per-scene optimization.

title: I2Mole: Interaction-aware Invariant Molecular Learning For Generalizable Property Prediction

AI.tldr: This paper proposes I2Mole, an interaction-aware invariant molecular learning framework that models intermolecular atomic interactions via a merged-graph information bottleneck and environment codebook for generalizable property prediction.
AI.motivation: Existing molecular property prediction models often neglect explicit modeling of molecular pairs and interactions, limiting their ability to capture core invariant substructures and generalize across diverse chemical environments.
AI.method: I2Mole connects intermolecular atoms in a merged graph, refines them using an improved graph information bottleneck tailored for merged graphs, and constructs an environment codebook from environment subgraphs to optimize mutual information while preserving chemical semantics.
AI.result: Extensive experimental validation demonstrates the efficacy and generalizability of I2Mole for molecular property prediction.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling intermolecular interactions with an environment-aware information bottleneck improves both interpretability and generalization in molecular learning.

title: Verification and Co-Alignment via Heterogeneous Consistency for Preference-Aligned LLM Annotations

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Heterogeneous-Consistency Co-Alignment (HCC), a training-free annotation framework that pairs an LLM with a lightweight specialist model to improve preference alignment across eight NLU datasets.
AI.motivation: Acquiring subjective, evolving, and culturally customizable preference annotations for LLMs via SFT or personalized RLHF is costly and labor-intensive.
AI.method: HCC pairs a knowledge-rich LLM with a task-specialized lightweight model guided by a small user preference set, using the reference-free Consistent-And-Inconsistent (CAI) Ratio to flag disagreements and a non-parametric embedding-based scheme to recalibrate inconsistent samples.
AI.result: Across eight NLU datasets and open- and closed-source LLMs, HCC improves annotation alignment, enables Llama-3-8B to surpass GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o-mini on several tasks, and shows that CAI strongly correlates with accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Heterogeneous model agreement provides an effective, reference-free signal for training-free, preference-aligned LLM annotation.

title: PathChat-SegR1: Reasoning Segmentation in Pathology via SO-GRPO

AI.tldr: This paper presents PathChat-SegR1, a pathology reasoning segmentation model trained with stain-invariant self-distillation and SO-GRPO, achieving a 61% zero-shot improvement over state-of-the-art models.
AI.motivation: Existing reasoning segmentation models fail on out-of-domain pathology images because their vision encoders lack stain-robust pathology knowledge, their LLMs struggle to decide when enough context is gathered to segment, and no pathology reasoning segmentation benchmark exists.
AI.method: PathChat-SegR1 uses a pathology-specific vision encoder trained with stain-invariant self-distillation, introduces Segmentation-Optimized GRPO (SO-GRPO) to learn optimal segmentation timing from accumulated reasoning context, and is evaluated on a new 118,667-triplet pathology reasoning segmentation benchmark.
AI.result: Zero-shot evaluation on out-of-domain tissue morphologies and pathologies demonstrates a 61% improvement over state-of-the-art segmentation models.
AI.conclusion: Combining stain-invariant visual representations with context-aware reinforcement learning for segmentation timing enables strong zero-shot generalization in pathology.

title: Let's Explore Step by Step: Generating Provable Formal Statements with Deductive Exploration

AI.tldr: This paper introduces DExploration, a Lean 4-verified deductive exploration framework for formal mathematical problem synthesis that boosts generation success from 40.70% to 54.52% while cutting token costs by 83%.
AI.motivation: Existing mathematical problem synthesis methods face an expressiveness-validity-complexity trilemma, often lacking whole-process verifiability, domain generality, or independence from external models.
AI.method: DExploration formulates synthesis as step-by-step deductive exploration with three Lean 4-verified atomic actions (introducing variables/hypotheses, deducing facts, submitting derived facts), bootstrapped via Exploratory Transformation that distills formal proofs into topologically ordered exploration trajectories.
AI.result: Experiments show DExploration improves success rate from 40.70% to 54.52% and reduces token cost from 52.9K to 8.8K (83% reduction), while generating 2,726 valid problems on which three state-of-the-art provers fail on 60 (Pass@4) and 8 (Pass@64).
AI.conclusion: Formal deductive exploration verified by Lean 4 resolves the expressiveness-validity-complexity trilemma for scalable, provable mathematical problem synthesis.

title: Uncertainty-Aware 3D Reconstruction for Dynamic Underwater Scenes

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an Uncertainty-aware Dynamic Field (UDF) using 4D neural voxels and per-pixel uncertainty modeling for dynamic underwater 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis.
AI.motivation: Underwater 3D reconstruction is hindered by light scattering, temporal scene dynamics, and observation noise, which rigid scene assumptions fail to capture.
