AI.method: UDF initializes a canonical underwater representation with 3D Gaussians in a volumetric medium field, maps it to a 4D neural voxel space with deformation and medium offset networks, and incorporates per-pixel uncertainty (from surface-view radiance ambiguity and inter-frame scene flow inconsistency) into the rendering loss.
AI.result: Experiments on controlled and in-the-wild underwater datasets show that UDF achieves high-quality 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis.
AI.conclusion: Jointly modeling dynamic scene geometry, time-varying medium properties, and observation uncertainty enables robust underwater 3D reconstruction.

title: ROSETTA: Constructing Code-Based Reward from Unconstrained Language Preference

AI.tldr: ROSETTA uses foundation models to translate unconstrained natural language preferences into multi-stage reward functions via code generation, enabling online RL adaptation for embodied agents with an 87% average success rate.
AI.motivation: Embodied agents must align with individual human preferences, but natural language preferences are unconstrained, diverse, and dynamic, and prior methods require extensive offline training or single-task fine-grained corrections.
AI.method: The framework uses foundation models to ground and disambiguate unconstrained natural language preferences, construct multi-stage reward functions, and implement them through code generation for online reinforcement learning adaptation.
AI.result: Tested on short-horizon and long-horizon manipulation tasks with human evaluation, ROSETTA outperforms SOTA baselines and achieves an 87% average success rate and 86% human satisfaction across 116 preferences.
AI.conclusion: ROSETTA enables embodied agents to adapt online to evolving and diverse human language preferences without offline reward model training.

title: SSVPO: Effective Step-Level Credit Assignment for RL Training of Language Models

AI.tldr: SSVPO introduces Sequential Shapley Values in an insertion MDP to perform fair step-level credit assignment for RL training of language models, improving accuracy by up to 11.6% and reducing token usage by 18.1%.
AI.motivation: Outcome-based RL for LLM mathematical reasoning is inefficient due to sparse final rewards, while existing credit assignment methods struggle to fairly evaluate individual steps in partially correct reasoning chains.
AI.method: Inspired by multi-agent RL, Sequential Shapley Value Policy Optimization (SSVPO) defines an insertion MDP and computes Sequential Shapley Values by reordering reasoning steps into alternative chains, using SSV as a PPO-consistent advantage baseline and pruning zero-credit steps.
AI.result: Across 7 benchmarks, SSVPO outperforms outcome-based (RLOO, GRPO, DAPO) and credit assignment-based (VinePPO, SPO) baselines, achieving up to an 11.6% accuracy gain, 18.1% token reduction, and 1.6x reasoning efficiency improvement over vanilla methods.
AI.conclusion: SSVPO provides theoretically fair step-level credit assignment that boosts post-training LLM reasoning performance while shortening reasoning chains and reducing token budgets.

title: Frequency-Balanced Retinal Representation Learning with Mutual Information Regularization

AI.tldr: RetMAE augments masked autoencoders with a mutual-information regularizer to suppress low-frequency redundancy and emphasize diagnostically critical high-frequency structures in retinal images.
AI.motivation: Masked autoencoders (MAE) favor low-frequency content and under-encode high-frequency details where retinal pathology often manifests, limiting diagnostic performance in ophthalmic modeling.
AI.method: Within a mutual-information formulation of MAE, the Frequency-Balanced Retinal Masked Autoencoder (RetMAE) adds an MI regularizer to the reconstruction objective without altering the underlying architecture.
AI.result: RetMAE learns frequency-balanced features that surpass MAE-based retinal encoders in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations.
AI.conclusion: A frequency-oriented perspective with a simple MI-based correction addresses ViT's low-pass bias in retinal images and provides a principled foundation for ophthalmic representation learning.

title: PAC-Bayes bounds for cumulative loss in Continual Learning

AI.tldr: This paper extends PAC-Bayes bounds to continual learning, deriving general upper bounds on cumulative generalization loss and oracle bounds for Gibbs posteriors that yield non-vacuous vision bounds.
AI.motivation: Continual learning requires balancing forward transfer and forgetting, yet generally applicable upper bounds on learning plasticity and reliable risk certificates are scarce.
AI.method: The authors extend PAC-Bayes bounds from online learning and time-uniform offline learning to continual learning, deriving general cumulative generalization loss bounds for any task distribution and algorithm alongside oracle bounds for Gibbs posteriors.
AI.result: Empirical evaluations show the approach produces non-vacuous bounds on several continual learning vision problems and tight oracle bounds on linear regression tasks.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes the first general upper bound on learning plasticity for continual learning, providing formal risk certificates across arbitrary task distributions.

title: A Bayesian Nonparametric Framework for Private, Fair, and Balanced Tabular Data Synthesis

AI.tldr: This paper presents a Bayesian nonparametric conditional generative framework that enforces fairness and class balance for private tabular data synthesis, extending beyond binary protected attributes.
AI.motivation: Data synthesis in data-scarce environments risks reproducing biases and marginalizing underrepresented groups, while existing fairness-aware methods primarily focus on binary-valued sensitive attributes.
AI.method: The framework fuses a conditional generator with Bayesian nonparametric learning (BNPL), imposing fairness by minimizing mutual information between generated outcomes and non-binary protected attributes while addressing class imbalance.
AI.result: Theoretical guarantees and extensive experiments on sensitive empirical examples demonstrate scalable, privacy-preserving, and equitable tabular data generation with adequate representation of underrepresented groups.
AI.conclusion: Combining conditional generation with Bayesian nonparametric learning offers a principled and scalable solution for private, fair, and balanced tabular data synthesis.

title: Expertise Can Be Helpful for Reinforcement Learning-based Macro Placement

AI.tldr: This paper integrates EDA expert knowledge and iterative post-refinement imitation into RL-based chip macro placement, improving total negative slack by 32.53% and worst negative slack by 7.74% over the runner-up.
AI.motivation: Existing RL-based macro placement methods neglect accumulated EDA engineering expertise and optimize oversimplified proxy objectives, leading to suboptimal PPA metrics compared to expert designs.
AI.method: The framework combines Expert Knowledge Injection (dataflow guidance, periphery bias, macro grouping, I/O keepout constraints) with Expert Workflow Imitation, which iteratively updates designs based on backend PPA feedback using preference optimization.
AI.result: On the ICCAD 2015 and OpenROAD benchmarks, the method outperforms analytical, black-box optimization, and RL-based baselines, improving total negative slack by 32.53% and worst negative slack by 7.74% on average over the runner-up.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating domain expertise and expert refinement workflows into RL substantially improves timing and PPA metrics in automated chip macro placement.

title: Point-UQ: An Uncertainty-Quantification Paradigm for Point Cloud Few-Shot Class Incremental Learning

AI.tldr: Point-UQ is a training-free uncertainty-quantification paradigm for 3D few-shot class-incremental learning that dynamically arbitrates between semantic classifiers and geometric prototypes, outperforming SOTA by 4% average accuracy.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D FSCIL methods fine-tune feature representations while keeping static decision boundaries, causing a trade-off between catastrophic forgetting of base classes and overfitting to novel classes.
AI.method: Point-UQ pairs Attention-driven Adaptive Enhancement (AAE), which fuses multi-scale features to compute calibrated prediction entropy, with Uncertainty-quantification Decision Decoupling (UDD), which uses that entropy to dynamically arbitrate between semantic classifiers and geometric prototypes without retraining.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on ModelNet, ShapeNet, ScanObjectNN, and CO3D show Point-UQ outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 4% in average accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Shifting from feature fine-tuning to uncertainty-guided dynamic decision optimization enables robust base-class retention and accurate novel-class recognition in 3D FSCIL.

title: Offline Preference-Based Value Optimization

AI.tldr: Preference-based Value Optimization (PVO) solves offline preference-based RL by minimizing a value alignment loss, achieving rate-optimal O(eps^-2) sample complexity and strong empirical performance without extra preference hyperparameters.
AI.motivation: Existing offline preference-based RL algorithms either rely on computationally intractable optimization or suffer from unstable training and high performance variance.
AI.method: PVO directly optimizes the value function to align with trajectory-pair preference feedback by minimizing a novel value alignment loss, which is applicable to both value-based and actor-critic algorithms.
AI.result: PVO is proven to achieve O(eps^-2) sample complexity and consistently outperforms strong baselines across continuous control benchmarks with stable training and no extra preference hyperparameters; ablations confirm replacing TD loss with value alignment loss substantially improves learning.
AI.conclusion: PVO bridges theory and practice in offline PbRL by offering a simple, hyperparameter-free, and rate-optimal value alignment objective.

title: Sequential Information Bottleneck Fusion: Towards Robust and Generalizable Multi-Modal Brain Tumor Segmentation

AI.tldr: Sequential Multi-modal Segmentation Network (SMSN) uses an Information-Bottleneck Fusion Module for sequential multi-modal MRI fusion, improving brain tumor segmentation under missing modalities and cross-domain transfer.
AI.motivation: Parallel fusion strategies for multi-modal MRI brain tumor segmentation risk losing shared information across modalities, degrading performance when one or more modalities are missing.
AI.method: Grounded in an information-theoretic analysis showing sequential fusion yields a tighter generalization upper bound, SMSN integrates an Information-Bottleneck Fusion Module (IBFM) to sequentially extract modality-common features while reconstructing modality-specific features.
AI.result: On BRATS18 and BRATS20, SMSN consistently outperforms parallel fusion baselines across diverse missing-modality settings and transfers from BRATS20 to a brain metastasis dataset without fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: Sequential information bottleneck fusion provides a theoretically grounded and robust approach to missing-modality multi-modal medical image segmentation and cross-domain generalization.

title: Value Matching: Scalable and Gradient-Free Reward-Guided Flow Adaptation

AI.tldr: Value Matching (VM) is an online optimal-control algorithm for reward-guided adaptation of flow and diffusion models that matches fine-tuning performance using less than 5% of the memory.
AI.motivation: Fine-tuning large flow and diffusion models via RL or optimal control incurs prohibitive memory costs, while offline Classifier Guidance suffers from limited reward expressivity and train-test distribution mismatch.
AI.method: VM learns the value function online within an optimal control setting, decoupling value network complexity from the base model, supporting non-differentiable rewards, and operating on-policy to explore high-reward regions beyond the data distribution.
AI.result: Across image generation and molecular design tasks, VM improves stability and sample efficiency over Classifier Guidance and achieves performance comparable to fine-tuning while using less than 5% of the memory.
AI.conclusion: Value Matching enables scalable, gradient-free, and memory-efficient reward-guided adaptation for large-scale flow and diffusion models.

title: Differentiable JPEG-based Input Perturbation for Knowledge Distillation Amplification via Conditional Mutual Information Maximization

AI.tldr: Differentiable JPEG-based Input Perturbation (DJIP) inserts a trainable JPEG layer before a frozen teacher network to maximize conditional mutual information, improving knowledge distillation accuracy by up to 4.11%.
AI.motivation: Maximizing conditional mutual information (CMI) improves teacher networks in knowledge distillation, but prior work requires fine-tuning large teachers or relying on inaccurate proxy objectives.
AI.method: DJIP places a plug-and-play differentiable JPEG layer before the teacher to perturb its inputs and uses an alternating optimization algorithm to learn JPEG coding parameters that directly maximize perturbed CMI without modifying the teacher.
AI.result: On CIFAR-100 and ImageNet across diverse distillers and architectures, DJIP consistently improves student accuracy by up to 4.11% while remaining lightweight and compatible with standard KD pipelines.
AI.conclusion: Input-space perturbation via differentiable JPEG coding offers an effective, teacher-agnostic way to amplify knowledge distillation.

title: PRISM: Partial-label Relational Inference with Spatial and Spectral Cues

AI.tldr: PRISM is a partial-label graph learning framework that combines spatial substructure alignment and multi-band spectral attention into a hybrid relational graph for iterative label propagation.
AI.motivation: Acquiring exact graph labels is costly, leading to partial-label graph learning where ambiguous candidate label sets hinder semantic extraction and cause overfitting to noisy labels.
AI.method: PRISM captures spatial cues via prototype-guided substructure alignment across graphs and global spectral cues via multi-frequency-band decomposition with attention, integrating both into a hybrid relational graph for candidate-constrained iterative label propagation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets show PRISM consistently outperforms strong baselines under various label noise settings.
AI.conclusion: Combining spatial and spectral relational inference effectively mitigates label ambiguity in partial-label graph learning.

title: Paradigm Shift of GNN Explainer from Label Space to Prototypical Representation Space

AI.tldr: IDEA is a dual-stage GNN explainer optimization framework that shifts alignment from label space to a prototypical graph representation space, improving ROC-AUC by 4.45% and precision by 48.71% on average.
AI.motivation: Existing post-hoc GNN explainers align input and explanation predictions in the graph label space, which lacks structural expressiveness, and face substructure entanglement and distributional discrepancy when moving to representation space.
AI.method: IDEA operates in two stages: Structural Information Disentanglement uses a graph tokenizer with a structure-aware objective to isolate explanatory substructures into prototypes, and Explanatory Prototype Alignment aligns input and explanation distributions in that prototypical space.
AI.result: Across real-world and synthetic datasets, IDEA improves ROC-AUC by 4.45% and precision by 48.71% on average, and boosts diverse existing explainer architectures by up to 10.70%.
AI.conclusion: Optimizing GNN explainers in a disentangled prototypical representation space overcomes the structural limitations of label-space alignment and generalizes across explainer architectures.

title: Latent-Guided Reasoning: Empowering Small LLMs with Large-Model Thinking

AI.tldr: Latent-Guided Reasoning decouples high-level planning in a large model from low-level execution in a small model via latent guidance vectors, boosting small LLM reasoning accuracy by up to 13.9%.
AI.motivation: Complex reasoning in LLMs is computationally expensive because high-level cognitive planning and low-level linguistic realization are tightly coupled in large models.
AI.method: A large Implicit Thinker compresses its solution strategy into compact latent guidance vectors, which a small Explicit Executor (0.5B to 8B) uses to generate concise reasoning chains, trained with an information-theoretic dual-loss objective including reconstruction loss.
AI.result: Across 8 reasoning benchmarks, the framework substantially improves small model reasoning and generalization across 0.5B to 8B scales, boosting accuracy by up to 13.9% over standalone baselines.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling planning and execution through latent guidance offers a theoretically grounded way to transfer large-model reasoning to small LLMs with a better performance-cost trade-off.

title: MaRS: Memory-Adaptive Routing for Reliable Capacity Expansion and Knowledge Retention

AI.tldr: MaRS is a modular continual learning framework for frozen large pre-trained models that combines statistically controlled slot expansion with contrastive-distillation adaptation to balance plasticity and retention.
AI.motivation: Continual learning with frozen large pre-trained models struggles with the stability-plasticity dilemma because shallow adaptation modules are prone to catastrophic forgetting.
AI.method: MaRS (Memory-adaptive Router with Statistical control) pairs a frozen encoder, a slot-based memory router, and a lightweight classifier, using Statistically-Grounded Slot Expansion (SGSE) for controlled growth with false-alarm/delay guarantees and Dual-Stage Contrastive-Distillation Adaptation (DCDA) to integrate new slots without raw replay.
AI.result: Experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate that MaRS achieves state-of-the-art continual learning performance with frozen LPMs, combining adaptability, efficiency, and knowledge retention.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling representation from statistically controlled memory routing enables reliable, replay-free capacity expansion in continual learning with frozen backbones.

title: OrthoSolver: A Neural Proper Orthogonal Decomposition Solver For PDEs

AI.tldr: OrthoSolver generalizes Proper Orthogonal Decomposition to nonlinear PDEs by maximizing mutual information with orthogonality regularization, outperforming deep learning baselines on seven PDE benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Classical POD is limited by linearity and fixed snapshot bases, while purely data-driven deep learning decomposition solvers lack physical priors and suffer from modal collapse.
AI.method: Establishing that POD's energy maximization is equivalent to maximizing mutual information, OrthoSolver iteratively and adaptively extracts nonlinear basis modes by maximizing mutual information with the data field under an orthogonality regularizer to prevent mode collapse.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on seven PDE benchmarks show OrthoSolver consistently outperforms state-of-the-art deep learning baselines.
AI.conclusion: Reformulating POD from an information-theoretic perspective provides a principled nonlinear neural solver that avoids modal collapse in PDE modeling.

title: Machine Learning Research Has Outpaced Its Communication Norms

AI.tldr: An analysis of 62,628 NeurIPS, ICLR, and ICML papers against arXiv and PubMed baselines reveals declining readability, an 80% rise in sensational language, and surging acronym density that LLM judges fail to detect.
AI.motivation: Machine learning research output has grown rapidly, raising the question of whether its communication norms and readability have degraded relative to other scientific fields.
AI.method: The authors evaluate NeurIPS (30,595 papers), ICLR (16,807), and ICML (15,226) against 2.8M arXiv and 24.3M PubMed baselines using classical readability scores, writing style metrics, acronym density/reuse, LLM judge ratings, and citation counts.
AI.result: Mean Flesch Reading Ease on NeurIPS abstracts dropped from ~24 (1987) to ~8 (2025), sensational language rose ~80% (2015-2025), title acronym density reached 3.5-4.2 per 100 words (88-90% appearing <10 times), LLM judges rated recent abstracts easier to read (contradicting 14/15 classical metrics), and top-cited decile papers read easier than bottom-decile papers on 12/15 metrics.
AI.conclusion: ML venues face a measurable, citation-compounding readability decline invisible to LLM judges, motivating seven measurable writing standards proposed for venue pilots.

title: Before Explicit Patch-Level Correspondence: A Controlled Audit of Aggregation in Cross-View Assembly-State Matching

AI.tldr: Controlled audits on IKEA-Bench D1 and Assembly101 show that adding simple patch-derived frame-similarity statistics to frozen DINOv2-L global descriptors recovers most of the accuracy gain of raw-patch composites without explicit patch correspondence.
AI.motivation: Frozen visual encoders struggle on cross-view assembly-state matching, raising the question of whether discriminative evidence is missing from the representation or merely underused by clip-global descriptors.
AI.method: Under a fixed frozen-encoder, product-disjoint protocol on IKEA-Bench D1 and Assembly101, the authors compare clip-global descriptors, global features plus spatially averaged frame-centroid similarity statistics, a raw-patch composite, and a supervised PartMetric.
AI.result: With frozen DINOv2-L on IKEA-Bench D1, clip-global reaches 58.29% accuracy, global plus frame-centroid statistics reaches 64.57%, and raw-patch composite reaches 66.86%; similar point-estimate orderings appear on DINOv2-B and Assembly101 subsets, though CLIP and video-to-manual matching do not reliably reproduce the pattern.
AI.conclusion: Simple patch-derived frame statistics capture much of the benefit of finer-grained descriptors in DINOv2 cross-view assembly-state matching, while highlighting clear limits across other encoders and settings.

title: An Axiomatic Framework for Transferability Metrics with Risk-Theoretic Grounding for Source-Model Selection

AI.tldr: This paper introduces four axioms for transferability metrics, proposes the Representation-Task Alignment (RTA) score, proves a Gaussian/LDA transfer risk bound, and shows RTA and CKA induce identical rankings across tested benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing transferability metrics (LEEP, LogME, H-Score) are heuristics without formal guarantees, leaving unanswered what foundational properties any compatibility metric should satisfy.
AI.method: The authors define four axioms (monotonicity, invariance, boundedness, consistency), propose the RTA score satisfying all four, prove an excess transfer risk bound in the Gaussian/LDA setting, and show LEEP, LogME, and H-Score are special cases or relaxations that violate at least one axiom.
AI.result: Across 20 pre-trained models and 15 VTAB-1k benchmarks (300 pairs), RTA and CKA are the only metrics with positive rank correlation on every dataset, outperforming LEEP, LogME, NCE, and H-Score; however, discriminative alignment saturates in 299/300 image pairs and 28/28 NLP pairs, making RTA and CKA produce identical rankings.
AI.conclusion: The work provides CKA with an axiomatic foundation it previously lacked, while identifying non-saturated regimes as future work to realize RTA's two-component advantage.

title: Style or Strategy? Discriminating Post-Training Displacement from Its Confounds in LLM Price Negotiation

AI.tldr: Controlled tests across three open LLM lineages in bilateral price negotiation reveal that apparent post-training strategic shifts are largely confounded by output-format failures, chat-template interfaces, and fixed stylistic anchoring rather than effective strategy.
AI.motivation: When aligned LLMs negotiate differently from base models, naive comparisons are confounded by unparseable output-format failures, late-turn failures, and fixed stylistic anchoring against single opponents.
AI.method: The authors design discriminating tests for each confound and run them across three open base->SFT->DPO(->RLVR) lineages in bilateral price negotiation, alongside an interface control crossing serialization with checkpoint and an accept-timing probe at horizon k=4.
AI.result: Output-format bands differ across families, openings do not track per-seller optima, concessions show no opponent-contingent adaptation by default, serialization affects OLMo stage attribution while Tulu's preference-stage locus persists, RLVR moves behavior less than earlier stages, and aligned models show accept-timing sensitivity at k=4 that earns essentially nothing.
AI.conclusion: No tested post-training channel exhibits effective negotiation strategy in this environment, underscoring the need to separate format-controlled displacement and contingent style from true strategic adaptation.

title: Optimal Transport Feature Alignment for Cross-Domain Cell Image Classification

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an unsupervised cross-domain single-cell classification pipeline using multi-encoder foundation features, shared-class filtering, graph-regularized optimal transport, and ensemble voting, improving average accuracy by 20%.
AI.motivation: Differences in microscope hardware, illumination, staining, and media cause severe domain shifts in computational cytology, degrading single-dataset models even when cell types overlap.
AI.method: The pipeline extracts features from multiple foundation encoders, unsupervisedly identifies shared cell types between datasets to filter unmatched classes, aligns embedding spaces via graph-regularized optimal transport (OT), and classifies via ensemble voting without target-domain fine-tuning.
AI.result: Across multiple real-world cell image datasets, adding class filtering and OT improves average accuracy by +20% and yields robust performance in both fully unsupervised and low-label regimes.
AI.conclusion: Filtering non-overlapping classes before graph-regularized optimal transport alignment enables accurate, training-free cross-domain single-cell classification.

title: Pragmatic Curiosity: A Unified Framework for Hybrid Learning and Optimization via Active Inference

AI.tldr: Pragmatic Curiosity (PraC) unifies Bayesian optimization and Bayesian experimental design via active inference by trading off latent information gain against expected regret-based outcome potential.
AI.motivation: Sequential decision-making under expensive black-box evaluations often requires both reducing uncertainty and optimizing task performance, yet Bayesian optimization and Bayesian experimental design treat these goals separately.
AI.method: PraC evaluates candidate queries by balancing information gain about a task-relevant latent symbol against an expected regret potential over outcomes, parameterized by latent choice, regret encoding, and exchange strength.
AI.result: Instantiated across decision-oriented monitoring, targeted active search, and composite Bayesian optimization with unknown preferences, PraC reduces downstream decision risk, improves critical-region coverage, and jointly learns predictive and preference structures without task-specific staging rules.
AI.conclusion: Active inference provides a unified, stage-free framework for hybrid learning and optimization across diverse sequential experimental settings.
